title.zh: 卷三十九 列傳第二十七: 薛安都 劉休賓 房法壽 畢眾敬 羊祉
title.en: Volume 39 Biographies 27: Xue Andou, Liu Xiubin, Fang Fashou, Bi Zhongjing, Yan Zhi
title.raw: 卷三十九 列傳第二十七: 薛安都 劉休賓 房法壽 畢眾敬 羊祉 Volume 39 Biographies 27: Xue Andou, Liu Xiubin, Fang Fashou, Bi Zhongjing, Yan Zhi

sentences.zh: 薛安都 劉休賓 房法壽 畢眾敬 羊祉

translations.literal: Xue Andou; Liu Xiubin; Fang Fashou; Bi Zhongjing; Yan Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andou, Liu Xiubin, Fang Fashou, Bi Zhongjing, and Yan Zhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十七

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty-Seven
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 27

sentences.zh: 薛安都劉休賓房法壽曾孫豹玄孫彥謙族子景伯畢眾敬曾孫義雲羊祉子深孫肅弟子敦烈

translations.literal: Xue Andou; Liu Xiubin; Fang Fashou, great-grandson Bao, great-great-grandson Yanqian, clansman Jingbo; Bi Zhongjing, great-grandson Yiyun; Yan Zhi, son Shen, grandson Su, nephew's son Dunlie
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andou; Liu Xiubin; Fang Fashou, his great-grandson Bao, his great-great-grandson Yanqian, and his clansman Jingbo; Bi Zhongjing, his great-grandson Yiyun; Yan Zhi, his son Shen, his grandson Su, and his nephew's son Dunlie

sentences.zh: 薛安都，字休達，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Andou, styled Xiuda, was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andou, styled Xiuda, came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父廣，晉上党太守。

translations.literal: His father Guang served as Administrator of Shangdang under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang had been Administrator of Shangdang in the Jin period.

sentences.zh: 安都少驍勇，善騎射，頗結輕俠，諸兄患之。

translations.literal: Andou in his youth was fierce and brave, skilled at horseback archery, and inclined to form ties with gallant ruffians; his elder brothers were troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Andou was bold and fierce, an expert horse archer who kept company with roaming blades; his older brothers worried about him.

sentences.zh: 安都乃求以一身分出，不取片資，兄許之，居於別廄。

translations.literal: Andou then asked to separate himself alone, taking not a shred of property; his brothers agreed, and he lived in a separate stable-yard.
translations.idiomatic: Andou asked to strike out on his own with nothing from the family estate; his brothers agreed, and he moved into a separate compound.

sentences.zh: 遠近交遊者爭有送遺，馬牛衣服什物充滿其庭。

translations.literal: Friends near and far vied to send him gifts; horses, oxen, clothing, and sundry goods filled his courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Companions from near and far showered him with gifts until horses, cattle, clothes, and household goods packed his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 真君五年，與東雍州刺史沮渠康謀逆，事發奔宋。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenjun, he plotted rebellion with Qu Ju Kang, Inspector of East Yongzhou; when the affair was exposed he fled to Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenjun he conspired to rebel with Qu Ju Kang, Inspector of East Yongzhou; when the plot was discovered he fled to the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 在南以武力見敘，遇宋孝武起江州，遂以為將。

translations.literal: In the south he was noted for martial prowess; when Emperor Xiaowu of Song rose in Jiangzhou, he was made a general.
translations.idiomatic: In the south his fighting ability won him notice, and when Emperor Xiaowu of Song raised forces in Jiangzhou, Andou was appointed a field commander.

sentences.zh: 和平六年，宋湘東王殺其主子業而自立，是為明帝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping, the Prince of Xiangdong of Song killed his lord Ziye and installed himself—that was Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Heping, the Prince of Xiangdong murdered his nephew the emperor Ziye and seized the throne as Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 群情不協，共立子業弟晉安王子勳。

translations.literal: Public sentiment was not in accord, and they jointly installed Ziye's younger brother, the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the court and provinces refused to accept Ming, and together they proclaimed Ziye's younger brother, the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun, as emperor.

sentences.zh: 安都與沈文秀、崔道固、常珍奇等舉兵應之。

translations.literal: Andou, with Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu, Chang Zhenqi, and others, raised troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Andou joined Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu, Chang Zhenqi, and others in taking up arms on Zixun's side.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝遺將張永討安都。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song sent the general Zhang Yong to attack Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming dispatched Zhang Yong to campaign against Andou.

sentences.zh: 安都遣使降魏，請兵救援，遣第四子道次為質。

translations.literal: Andou sent envoys to surrender to Wei and request military aid, sending his fourth son Daoci as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Andou sent envoys to submit to Northern Wei and beg for reinforcements, offering his fourth son Daoci as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 獻文乃遣鎮東大將軍尉元等赴之，拜安都鎮南大將軍、徐州刺史，賜爵河東公。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen then sent the Commander-in-chief of the East Yu Yuan and others to his aid, appointed Andou Defender-general of the South, Inspector of Xuzhou, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen sent Yu Yuan, Commander-in-chief of the East, and other officers to his relief, named Andou Defender-general of the South and Inspector of Xuzhou, and granted him the title Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 元等既入彭城，安都中悔，謀圖元等。

translations.literal: Once Yuan and the others had entered Pengcheng, Andou repented midway and plotted against Yuan and his men.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan's forces entered Pengcheng, Andou had second thoughts and plotted to turn on them.

sentences.zh: 元知之，遂不果發。

translations.literal: Yuan learned of it, and the plan was therefore not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan discovered the plot, and the coup never came off.

sentences.zh: 安都因重貨元等，委罪于女婿裴祖隆。

translations.literal: Andou thereupon lavished heavy gifts on Yuan and the others and pinned the guilt on his son-in-law Pei Zulong.
translations.idiomatic: Andou then bribed Yuan heavily and shifted the blame onto his son-in-law Pei Zulong.

sentences.zh: 元乃殺祖隆而隱安都謀。

translations.literal: Yuan then killed Zulong and concealed Andou's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan executed Zulong but kept Andou's role hidden.

sentences.zh: 皇興二年，與畢眾敬朝于京師，甚見禮重。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangxing, he went to court in the capital with Bi Zhongjing and was treated with great honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangxing he visited the capital with Bi Zhongjing and received lavish honors at court.

sentences.zh: 子侄群從並處上客，皆封侯，至於門生，無不收敘。

translations.literal: His sons, nephews, and collateral kin were all treated as honored guests and enfeoffed as marquises; even his private students were all given appointments.
translations.idiomatic: His sons, nephews, and kinsmen were all received as honored guests and enfeoffed as marquises, and even his personal pupils were given official posts.

sentences.zh: 又為起第宅，館宇崇麗，資給甚厚。

translations.literal: A mansion was also built for him, its halls lofty and splendid, with very generous provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The court also built him a residence with grand halls and supplied him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈假黃鉞、秦州刺史、河東王，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given the ceremonial axe, made Inspector of Qinzhou and King of Hedong, with the posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted the ceremonial axe, the inspectorship of Qinzhou, and the title King of Hedong, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 子道舣襲爵，位平州刺史，政有聲稱。

translations.literal: His son Daoyi inherited the title, served as Inspector of Pingzhou, and gained a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoyi inherited the title, became Inspector of Pingzhou, and earned a name for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 曆相、秦二州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He served successively as Inspector of Xiang and Qin provinces, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He held the inspectorships of Xiang and Qin in turn before his death.

sentences.zh: 道舣弟道異，亦以勳為第一客。

translations.literal: Daoyi's younger brother Daoyi was also made a foremost guest on account of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyi's younger brother Daoyi likewise became a foremost guest of the court by virtue of his family's service.

sentences.zh: 早卒，贈秦州刺史、安邑侯。

translations.literal: He died young and was posthumously made Inspector of Qinzhou and Marquis of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died young and was posthumously named Inspector of Qinzhou and Marquis of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 道異弟道次，既質京師，賜爵安邑侯，位秦州刺史，進河南公。

translations.literal: Daoyi's younger brother Daoci, having already been a hostage in the capital, was granted the title Marquis of Anyi, made Inspector of Qinzhou, and advanced to Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyi's younger brother Daoci, who had served as a hostage in the capital, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyi, appointed Inspector of Qinzhou, and later promoted to Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 安都從祖弟真度，初亦與安都南奔；

translations.literal: Andou's collateral cousin Zhendu had at first also fled south with Andou;
translations.idiomatic: Andou's collateral cousin Zhendu had likewise fled south with him at first;

sentences.zh: 及從安都來降，為上客。

translations.literal: when he followed Andou in surrendering he became an honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: and when he followed Andou in submitting to Wei he too was received as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 太和初，賜爵河北侯，出為平州刺史，假陽平公，後降為伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was granted the title Marquis of Hebei, sent out as Inspector of Pingzhou with acting rank as Duke of Yangping, and later reduced to a baron.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hebei, posted as Inspector of Pingzhou with acting rank as Duke of Yangping, and later demoted to baron.

sentences.zh: 曆荊州、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as Inspector of Jingzhou and East Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held the inspectorships of Jingzhou and East Jingzhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 初遷洛後，真度每獻計勸先取樊、鄧，後攻南陽，故大為帝所賞。

translations.literal: After the move to Luoyang, Zhendu repeatedly submitted plans urging that Fan and Deng be taken first and Nanyang attacked afterward, and for this he was greatly rewarded by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was moved to Luoyang, Zhendu repeatedly urged taking Fan and Deng first and only then striking Nanyang, and the emperor valued him highly for this counsel.

sentences.zh: 改封臨晉縣伯，轉豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Baron of Linjin County, and he was transferred to Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Baron of Linjin County and appointed Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 景明初，豫州大饑，真度表輒日別出倉米五十斛為粥，救其甚者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Yuzhou suffered a great famine; Zhendu memorialized that each day fifty hu of grain from the granary be set aside for porridge to save the worst afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingming, when Yuzhou was stricken by famine, Zhendu petitioned to issue fifty hu of grain from the storehouses each day for gruel kitchens to aid the most desperate.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「真度所表，甚有憂濟百姓之意，宜在拯恤。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Zhendu's memorial shows deep concern to relieve the people; he should be commended for succoring them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne responded: "Zhendu's report reflects genuine solicitude for the common people and deserves praise for relief work.

sentences.zh: 」曆華、荊二州刺史，入為大司農卿。

translations.literal: " He served sequentially as Inspector of Hua and Jing provinces, then entered court as Minister of the Grand Granary.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on to hold the inspectorships of Hua and Jing in turn, then was appointed Minister of the Grand Granary.

sentences.zh: 正始初，除揚州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was appointed Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengshi reign he was named Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，改封敷西。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was made Grand Master of the Golden Chariot with Purple Tassel, given the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and his fief was changed to Fuxi.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court he was appointed Grand Master of the Golden Chariot with Purple Tassel and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and his fief was changed to Fuxi.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左光祿大夫，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously named Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 有子十二人，嫡子懷徹襲封。

translations.literal: He had twelve sons; his legitimate son Huaiche inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He had twelve sons; his legitimate heir Huaiche succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 初，真度有女妓數十人。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhendu had several dozen female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: In his earlier years Zhendu kept several dozen female performers.

sentences.zh: 每集賓客，輒命之絲竹歌舞，不輟於前，盡聲色之適。

translations.literal: Whenever he gathered guests he would have them perform music and dance without pause before him, indulging fully in sensual pleasures.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entertained guests he had them perform music and dance without cease, reveling in every pleasure of sight and sound.

sentences.zh: 庶長子懷吉，居喪過周，以父妓十餘人並樂器獻之，宣武納焉。

translations.literal: His eldest son by a concubine, Huaiji, after the mourning period had passed the full cycle, presented more than ten of his father's entertainers together with their instruments; Emperor Xuanwu accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son by a concubine, Huaiji, after completing the full mourning cycle presented more than ten of his father's performers along with their instruments, and Emperor Xuanwu took them into the palace.

sentences.zh: 懷吉好勇，有膂力，雖不善書學，亦解達時事。

translations.literal: Huaiji loved valor and had great physical strength; though not skilled in letters, he also understood current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiji loved fighting and was powerfully built; though no scholar, he had a keen grasp of practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒于汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office as Inspector of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Inspector of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷吉本不厲清節，及為汾州，偏有聚納之響。

translations.literal: Huaiji had never been strict in integrity; once he became Inspector of Fenzhou he gained a reputation especially for amassing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiji had never been known for integrity, and as Inspector of Fenzhou he became notorious for extortion and hoarding.

sentences.zh: 自以支庶，餌誘勝己，共為婚姻。

translations.literal: Considering himself a lesser branch of the family, he courted and enticed those of higher standing, arranging marriages with them.
translations.idiomatic: As a cadet line he flattered men of higher rank and sealed alliances through marriage.

sentences.zh: 多攜親戚，悉令同行，兼為之彌縫，恣其取受。

translations.literal: He often brought along kinsmen and had them all travel with him, while also smoothing over matters for them and letting them take and accept as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He often took relatives along on his tours of office and covered for their abuses, letting them take what they wanted.

sentences.zh: 而將勞賓客，曲盡物情，送去迎來，不避寒熱。

translations.literal: Yet in receiving and entertaining guests he exhausted every courtesy, seeing them off and welcoming them in without shunning heat or cold.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with guests he was tirelessly hospitable, seeing them off and welcoming them in without regard for weather.

sentences.zh: 性少言，每有接對，但默然而返。

translations.literal: By nature he spoke little; whenever he received someone he would only return in silence.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of few words and would often receive guests in silence and send them away without comment.

sentences.zh: 既指授先期明人馬之數，左右密已記錄。

translations.literal: Yet beforehand he had already indicated the number of men and horses required, and his attendants had secretly recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet beforehand he had quietly specified how many men and horses would be needed, and his staff had already noted it down.

sentences.zh: 俄而酒饌相尋，芻粟繼至，逮於將別，贈以錢縑，下及廝庸，咸過本望。

translations.literal: Soon wine and food followed in succession, fodder and grain arrived one after another, and when they were about to part he gave them money and silk; even down to servants and laborers, all received more than they had hoped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon feasts and fodder arrived in steady streams, and when guests departed he lavished money and silk on them—even servants and grooms received more than they had dared expect.

sentences.zh: 真度諸子既多，其母非一；

translations.literal: Zhendu had many sons, and their mothers were not one;
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu had many sons by different mothers;

sentences.zh: 同產相朋，因有憎愛。

translations.literal: those of the same mother banded together, and thus there arose hatred and favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: and sons who shared a mother formed factions, breeding mutual hatred and favoritism.

sentences.zh: 興和中，遂致訴列，雲以毒藥相害。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era they finally brought lawsuits against one another, alleging mutual poisoning.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xinghe era they finally sued one another in open court, each accusing the others of poisoning.

sentences.zh: 顯在公府，發揚疵釁，時人恥焉。

translations.literal: The scandal was displayed in the public offices and their faults aired; people of the time were shamed by it.
translations.idiomatic: The affair played out in the public courts with every family stain exposed, to the shame of all who heard of it.

sentences.zh: 劉休賓，字處幹，本平原人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiubin, styled Chugan, was originally a native of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiubin, styled Chugan, was originally from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖昶，從慕容德度河，家于北海都昌縣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang, following Murong De in crossing the river, settled his family in Duchang County of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang had crossed the Yellow River with Murong De and settled the family in Duchang County in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 父奉伯，宋北海太守。

translations.literal: His father Fengbo served as Administrator of Beihai under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fengbo had been Administrator of Beihai under the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 休賓少好學，有文才。

translations.literal: Xiubin in his youth loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin loved study from youth and showed real literary talent.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He served Song as Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Liu Song as Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 娶崔邪利女，生子文曄。

translations.literal: He married the daughter of Cui Xieli and had a son Wenhua.
translations.idiomatic: He married a daughter of Cui Xieli and fathered a son named Wenhua.

sentences.zh: 崔氏先歸甯在魯郡。

translations.literal: The Cui woman had earlier returned to her natal home and was staying in Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui had earlier gone home to her family and was staying in Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 邪利之降，文曄母子與俱入魏。

translations.literal: When Xieli surrendered, Wenhua and his mother entered Wei together with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xieli submitted to Wei, Wenhua and his mother went north with him.

sentences.zh: 及慕容白曜軍至，休賓不降。

translations.literal: When Murong Baiyao's army arrived, Xiubin would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Baiyao's army arrived, Xiubin refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 白曜請崔氏與文曄至，以報休賓。

translations.literal: Baiyao requested that Lady Cui and Wenhua be brought forward to inform Xiubin.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao had Lady Cui and Wenhua brought before the walls to show Xiubin.

sentences.zh: 又執休賓兄延和妻子巡視城下。

translations.literal: He also seized the wife and children of Xiubin's elder brother Yanhe and paraded them below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He also took the wife and children of Xiubin's elder brother Yanhe and marched them along the base of the walls.

sentences.zh: 休賓答白曜，許待曆城降，當即歸順。

translations.literal: Xiubin replied to Baiyao, promising that once Licheng surrendered he would at once submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin answered Baiyao that he would submit as soon as Licheng fell.

sentences.zh: 密遣主簿尹文達向曆城，觀魏軍形勢。

translations.literal: He secretly sent his Registrar Yin Wenda toward Licheng to observe the Wei army's disposition.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent his Registrar Yin Wenda to Licheng to scout the Wei forces.

sentences.zh: 文達詣白曜，詐祗侯。

translations.literal: Wenda went to Baiyao and pretended to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Wenda called on Baiyao and feigned deference.

sentences.zh: 白曜令文達往升城，見其妻子。

translations.literal: Baiyao had Wenda go up to the city to see his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao sent Wenda up to the city to see his family.

sentences.zh: 文曄哭泣，以爪發為信。

translations.literal: Wenhua wept and sent a token made from his fingernails and hair.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua wept and sent a token of his fingernails and hair.

sentences.zh: 文達回，復經白曜，誓約而還，見休賓。

translations.literal: Wenda returned, again passed by Baiyao, swore an oath, and went back to see Xiubin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenda returned by way of Baiyao's camp, exchanged sworn pledges, and reported to Xiubin.

sentences.zh: 休賓撫爪發泣，復遣文達與白曜期。

translations.literal: Xiubin stroked the nails and hair and wept, then again sent Wenda to fix a date with Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin clutched the token and wept, then sent Wenda again to set a date with Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 白曜喜，以酒灌地，啟告山河，誓不負休賓。

translations.literal: Baiyao rejoiced, poured wine upon the ground, addressed the mountains and rivers, and swore not to betray Xiubin.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao rejoiced, poured a libation to earth and heaven, and swore before the spirits of the land that he would not betray Xiubin.

sentences.zh: 文達還謂休賓，可早決計。

translations.literal: Wenda returned and told Xiubin he should decide quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Wenda urged Xiubin to make up his mind at once.

sentences.zh: 休賓於是告兄子聞慰。

translations.literal: Xiubin thereupon informed his nephew Wenwei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin then told his nephew Wenwei.

sentences.zh: 聞慰固執不可，遂差本契。

translations.literal: Wenwei stubbornly refused, and thus the original pact was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei adamantly refused, and the original agreement fell apart.

sentences.zh: 白曜尋遣著作佐郎許赤彪夜至梁鄒南門，告城上人曰：「休賓遣文達頻造僕射許降，何得無信！

translations.literal: Baiyao soon sent the Assistant Editor of Writings Xu Chibiao by night to the south gate of Liangzou, telling those atop the wall: "Xiubin sent Wenda repeatedly to the Vice Director to promise surrender—how can there be no good faith!
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao soon sent the Assistant Editor of Writings Xu Chibiao by night to the south gate of Liangzou and called up to the defenders: "Xiubin has sent Wenda again and again to my chief of staff to promise surrender—where is your good faith!

sentences.zh: 」於是城內遂相維持，欲降不得。

translations.literal: " Thereupon within the city they restrained one another, wishing to surrender but unable to.
translations.idiomatic: " At that the garrison turned on one another, each faction blocking the others from surrendering.

sentences.zh: 曆城降，休賓乃出請命。

translations.literal: When Licheng surrendered, Xiubin then came out to beg for his life.
translations.idiomatic: When Licheng fell, Xiubin came out to submit.

sentences.zh: 及立平齊郡，乃以梁鄒人為懷寧縣，以休賓為令。

translations.literal: When Pingqi Commandery was established, the people of Liangzou were made Huaining County, and Xiubin was made its magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingqi Commandery was established, the district of Liangzou was organized as Huaining County and Xiubin was appointed its magistrate.

sentences.zh: 延興二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yanxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yanxing.

sentences.zh: 文曄有志尚，綜覽群書，輕財重義。

translations.literal: Wenhua had lofty aspirations, surveyed many books, held wealth lightly and valued righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua was a man of high purpose who read widely, scorned wealth, and prized loyalty.

sentences.zh: 太和中，坐從兄聞慰南叛，被徙北邊，孝文特聽還代。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, because his cousin Wenwei rebelled in the south he was exiled to the northern frontier; Emperor Xiaowen specially permitted him to return to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe reign he was banished to the northern frontier because his cousin Wenwei had defected south; Emperor Xiaowen specially allowed him to return to Dai.

sentences.zh: 帝曾幸方山，文曄大言求見，申父功厚賞屈。

translations.literal: When the emperor once visited Fangshan, Wenhua spoke loudly seeking an audience, stating that his father's merits had been richly rewarded while his own rewards were slight.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Fangshan, Wenhua called out for an audience, protesting that his father's great service had been richly honored while he himself had been slighted.

sentences.zh: 於是賜爵都昌子，深見待遇，拜協律中郎。

translations.literal: He was thereupon granted the title Viscount of Duchang, treated with deep favor, and appointed Harmonist-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then enfeoffed him as Viscount of Duchang, showed him marked favor, and appointed him Harmonist-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 卒于高陽太守，贈兗州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died as Administrator of Gaoyang and was posthumously made Inspector of Yanzhou, with the posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Administrator of Gaoyang and was posthumously named Inspector of Yanzhou, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 休賓叔父旋之，其妻許氏生二子法鳳、法武，而旋之早卒。

translations.literal: Xiubin's uncle Xuanzhi—his wife Lady Xu bore two sons, Fafeng and Fawu—and Xuanzhi died young.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin's uncle Xuanzhi, whose wife Lady Xu bore two sons, Fafeng and Fawu, died young.

sentences.zh: 東陽平，許氏攜二子入魏，孤貧不自立，母子並出家為尼僧。

translations.literal: When Dongyang was pacified, Lady Xu brought the two sons into Wei; destitute and unable to support themselves, mother and sons all left home to become Buddhist nuns.
translations.idiomatic: After Dongyang was pacified, Lady Xu brought the two boys north; too poor to survive on their own, mother and sons all took Buddhist vows as nuns.

sentences.zh: 既而反俗，俱奔江南。

translations.literal: Later they returned to lay life and together fled to the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: They later returned to lay life and fled together to the south.

sentences.zh: 法武后改名峻，字孝標，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: Fawu later changed his name to Jun, styled Xiaobiao; he has a biography in the "History of the Southern Dynasties."
translations.idiomatic: Fawu later changed his name to Jun, styled Xiaobiao, and is the subject of a biography in the "History of the Southern Dynasties."

sentences.zh: 房法壽，小名烏頭，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Fang Fashou, whose childhood name was Wutou, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fashou, childhood name Wutou, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 曾祖諶，仕燕，位太尉掾。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chen served Yan as an aide in the office of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chen had served the Yan state as an aide in the Grand Commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 隨慕容氏遷于齊，子孫因家之，遂為東清河繹幕人焉。

translations.literal: Following the Murong clan's move to Qi, his descendants settled there and thus became natives of Yimu in East Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: When the Murong clan moved to Qi the family settled there, and his line became natives of Yimu in East Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 法壽幼孤，少好射獵，輕率勇果，結諸群小為劫盜，宗族患之。

translations.literal: Fashou was orphaned young; in his youth he loved hunting, was rash and bold, and joined with various low fellows in banditry; his clan was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Fashou loved the hunt, was reckless and fierce, and ran with a gang of petty thieves until his kinsmen despaired of him.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州迎主簿。

translations.literal: At his capping he was welcomed by the province as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping ceremony the province invited him to serve as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 後以母老，不復應州郡命，常盜殺豬羊以供母。

translations.literal: Later, because his mother was old, he no longer responded to provincial and commandery appointments, and often stole pigs and sheep to supply his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his mother grew old, he declined all provincial appointments and routinely stole pigs and sheep to feed her.

sentences.zh: 招集壯士，恆有數百。

translations.literal: He gathered strong men; he always had several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered stalwart fighters and kept several hundred at his command.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He served Song as Administrator of Weijun.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Liu Song as Administrator of Weijun.

sentences.zh: 法壽從祖弟崇吉，母妻為慕容白曜所獲，托法壽為計，法壽與崇吉歸款于白曜。

translations.literal: Fashou's younger second cousin Chongji—his mother and wife having been captured by Murong Baiyao—entrusted Fashou to devise a plan; Fashou and Chongji submitted in good faith to Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji, Fashou's younger second cousin, had lost his mother and wife to Murong Baiyao's forces and turned to Fashou for a plan; together they surrendered to Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 詔以法壽為平遠將軍，與韓騏驎對為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Fashou General Who Pacifies the Distance and paired him with Han Qilin as Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Fashou General Who Pacifies the Distance and named him and Han Qilin co-inspectors of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 及曆城、梁鄒降，法壽、崇吉等與崔道固、劉休賓俱至京師。

translations.literal: When Licheng and Liangzou surrendered, Fashou, Chongji, and the others arrived at the capital together with Cui Daogu and Liu Xiubin.
translations.idiomatic: After Licheng and Liangzou fell, Fashou and Chongji went to the capital alongside Cui Daogu and Liu Xiubin.

sentences.zh: 以法壽為上客，崇吉為次客，崔、劉為下客。

translations.literal: Fashou was treated as a senior guest, Chongji as a secondary guest, and Cui and Liu as junior guests.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou was received as a guest of highest rank, Chongji as second rank, and Cui and Liu as the lowest.

sentences.zh: 法壽供給亞于薛安都等，以功賜爵壯武侯，給以田宅奴婢。

translations.literal: Fashou's provisions were second only to those of Xue Andou and the like; for his merit he was granted the title Marquis of Zhuangwu and given fields, dwellings, and slave attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His upkeep at court ranked just below Xue Andou's; for his service he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuangwu and given land, a house, and household slaves.

sentences.zh: 性愛酒，好施，親舊賓客率同饑飽，坎壈常不豐足。

translations.literal: By nature he loved wine and was fond of giving; with kin, old friends, and guests he generally shared hunger and fullness alike, and his hardships often left him without abundance.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and was generous to a fault, sharing feast and famine alike with kinsmen and guests, and seldom kept himself comfortably supplied.

sentences.zh: 畢眾敬等皆尚其通愛。

translations.literal: Bi Zhongjing and others all admired his universal love.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhongjing and others all valued his openhanded warmth.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈青州刺史，諡敬侯。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Qingzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously named Inspector of Qingzhou and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子伯祖襲，例降為伯，曆齊郡內史。

translations.literal: His son Bozu inherited the title; by precedent it was reduced to a barony, and he served sequentially as Inner Scribe of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bozu succeeded to the title, which was reduced by precedent to a barony, and he served as Inner Scribe of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 伯祖訚弱，委事于功曹張僧皓，大有受納，伯祖衣食不充。

translations.literal: Bozu was weak and timid; he entrusted affairs to the Merit Officer Zhang Senghao, who greatly accepted bribes, and Bozu's food and clothing were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Timid and ineffectual, Bozu turned the work over to his Merit Officer Zhang Senghao, who took heavy bribes while Bozu himself went without adequate food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 後卒于幽州輔國府長史，免官，卒。

translations.literal: Later he died as Chief Clerk of the Support-the-State Bureau in Youzhou; dismissed from office, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Chief Clerk of the Support-the-State Bureau in Youzhou; stripped of office, he died.

sentences.zh: 子翼，大城戍主，帶宗安太守，襲爵壯武侯。

translations.literal: His son Yi was garrison commandant of Dacheng and concurrently Administrator of Zong'an, inheriting the title Marquis of Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, garrison commandant of Dacheng and concurrently Administrator of Zong'an, succeeded to the title Marquis of Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 翼子豹，字仲幹。

translations.literal: Yi's son Bao, with the style name Zhonggan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Bao, styled Zhonggan.

sentences.zh: 體貌魁岸，美音儀。

translations.literal: His build was imposing and lofty, and his voice and bearing were fine.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and striking in appearance, with a pleasing voice and presence.

sentences.zh: 年十七，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: At age seventeen the province summoned him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he was recruited by the province as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 王思政入據潁川，慕容紹宗出討，豹為紹宗開府主簿兼行台郎中。

translations.literal: When Wang Sizheng entered and held Yingchuan, Murong Shaozong went out to suppress him; Bao served Shaozong as Chief Clerk of his headquarters and concurrently Secretary of the Mobile Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sizheng seized Yingchuan, Murong Shaozong marched out against him, and Bao became Shaozong's headquarters chief clerk and concurrent secretary on the mobile staff.

sentences.zh: 紹宗自雲有水厄，遂於戰艦中浴，並自投于水，冀以厭當之。

translations.literal: Shaozong himself said he had a water calamity and so bathed in a warship and even threw himself into the water, hoping to use apotropaic substitution to avert it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong believed himself fated to die by water and bathed aboard a warship, even throwing himself overboard in the hope of turning the omen aside.

sentences.zh: 豹白紹宗曰：「夫命也在天，豈人理所能延保。

translations.literal: Bao told Shaozong: "Fate lies with Heaven—how can human effort prolong or preserve life?
translations.idiomatic: Bao said to Shaozong, "Life and death are Heaven's decree—what mortal scheme could extend or preserve them?

sentences.zh: 公若實有水厄，非禳辟所能卻；

translations.literal: If you truly have a water calamity, it cannot be turned back by ritual warding;
translations.idiomatic: If you truly face a water doom, no rite of warding can turn it aside;

sentences.zh: 若其實無，何禳之有。

translations.literal: if in truth there is none, what is there to ward off?
translations.idiomatic: if there is no such doom, what is there to ward off at all?

sentences.zh: 今三軍之事，在於明公，唯應達命任理，以保元吉。

translations.literal: Now the affairs of the three armies rest with you, my lord; you should only accept fate and abide by reason to preserve the greatest good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies now depend on you, my lord; you need only accept fate and act by reason to preserve the greatest fortune.

sentences.zh: 方乃乘船入水，雲以防災，豈如岸上指麾，以保萬全也。

translations.literal: Yet now you board a ship and enter the water, saying it is to ward off disaster—how does that compare with commanding from the shore to preserve complete safety?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you board a ship and plunge into the water, claiming it wards off disaster—how can that compare with commanding from the shore and keeping every advantage?

sentences.zh: 」紹宗笑曰：「不能免俗，為復爾耳。

translations.literal: " Shaozong laughed and said: "One cannot escape vulgar custom—it is just the same again.
translations.idiomatic: " Shaozong laughed and said, "One cannot escape vulgar habit—it always comes to this.

sentences.zh: 」未幾而紹宗遇溺，時論以為知微。

translations.literal: " Before long Shaozong met with drowning; opinion at the time held that Bao had discerned the subtle sign.
translations.idiomatic: " Not long afterward Shaozong drowned, and contemporaries took it as proof of Bao's foresight.

sentences.zh: 清河中，除謁者僕射，拜西河太守。

translations.literal: In Qinghe he was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Reverence and invested as Administrator of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qinghe reign he was made Vice Director of the Masters of Reverence and Administrator of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 地接周境，俗雜稽胡，豹政貴清靜，甚著聲績。

translations.literal: The district bordered Zhou territory and its customs mixed with Jie and Hu peoples; Bao's government valued quiet simplicity and won great renown for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The district bordered Northern Zhou and its population mixed Han with tribal peoples; Bao governed with restraint and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 遷博陵太守，亦有能名。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Bolling and likewise had a name for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Bolling and earned renown there as well.

sentences.zh: 又遷樂陵太守，風教修理，稱為美政。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Administrator of Leling; he repaired customs and teaching, and his rule was praised as excellent government.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made Administrator of Leling, where he restored local customs and was praised for enlightened rule.

sentences.zh: 郡瀕海，水味多鹹苦。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered the sea, and its water tasted mostly salty and bitter.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery lay on the coast, and its water was mostly brackish and bitter.

sentences.zh: 豹命鑿一井，遂得甘泉，遐邇以為政化所致。

translations.literal: Bao ordered a well dug and obtained sweet spring water; near and far took it as the effect of his civilizing governance.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had a well sunk and struck sweet water; people near and far attributed it to the virtue of his rule.

sentences.zh: 豹罷歸後，井味復咸。

translations.literal: After Bao left office and returned home, the well's water again turned salty.
translations.idiomatic: After Bao resigned and went home, the well turned brackish again.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，遂還本鄉，丘園自養。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, he returned to his native district and nourished himself in hill and garden seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he returned to his home country and lived in quiet retirement.

sentences.zh: 頻被征命，固辭以疾。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly summoned by imperial appointment but firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated summonses reached him, but he steadfastly pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 每牧守初臨，必遣致禮，官佐邑宰皆投刺申敬。

translations.literal: Whenever a new provincial or commandery chief arrived, they invariably sent gifts of courtesy; his subordinate officials and district magistrates all presented calling cards to express respect.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a new prefect or commandery chief took up his post, he sent courtesies; local officials and magistrates all called to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 終於家，無子，以兄熊子彥詡嗣。

translations.literal: He died at home without sons; his elder brother Xiong's son Yanxu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home childless, and his nephew Yanxu, son of his elder brother Xiong, became his heir.

sentences.zh: 彥詡明辯有學識，位殿中侍御史，千乘、益都二縣令，有惠政。

translations.literal: Yanxu was bright in debate and possessed learning; he reached the post of Palace Attendant Censor, served as magistrate of both Qiansheng and Yidu counties, and had benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxu was eloquent and learned, rose to Palace Attendant Censor, served as magistrate of Qiansheng and Yidu, and governed with beneficence.

sentences.zh: 熊字子威，性至孝，聰郎有節概。

translations.literal: Xiong, styled Ziwei, was by nature profoundly filial, clever and bright (聰朗; 郎 is likely a variant), and possessed of integrity and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, styled Ziwei, was deeply filial by nature, quick and upright in mind, and firm in moral principle.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，行清河、廣川二郡事。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Chief Clerk, and he administered the affairs of Qinghe and Guangchuan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The province recruited him as Chief Clerk and put him in charge of Qinghe and Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 七子。

translations.literal: Seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 長子彥詢最知名，以魏勳門嫡孫，賜爵永始縣子，特為叔豹所愛重。

translations.literal: The eldest son Yanxun was the most renowned; as legitimate grandson of a meritorious Wei house he was granted the title Viscount of Yongshi County and was especially loved and honored by his uncle Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Yanxun, was the most celebrated; as the legitimate grandson of a Wei house honored for its service he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongshi County and was a particular favorite of his uncle Bao.

sentences.zh: 病卒，豹取急，親送柩還鄉；

translations.literal: He died of illness; Bao took emergency leave and personally escorted the coffin back to their native district;
translations.idiomatic: When illness took him, Bao obtained emergency leave and personally escorted the coffin home;

sentences.zh: 悲痛傷惜，以為喪當家之寶。

translations.literal: Grief-stricken and full of regret, Bao regarded the loss as bereft of the family's treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken with grief, Bao mourned him as though the family had lost its greatest treasure.

sentences.zh: 初，彥詢少時為監館，嘗接陳使江總。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanxun was young he served as lodge host and once received the Chen envoy Jiang Zong.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yanxun had served as host of the diplomatic lodge and once entertained the Chen envoy Jiang Zong.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，總入關，見彥詢弟彥謙曰：「公是監館弟邪？

translations.literal: When Chen perished, Zong entered the Pass and, meeting Yanxun's younger brother Yanqian, said: "Are you the younger brother of the lodge host?
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Zong entered the Pass and, meeting Yanxun's younger brother Yan Yanqian, said, "Are you the lodge host's younger brother?

sentences.zh: 」因慘然曰：「昔因將命，得申言款。

translations.literal: " Then, with a mournful air, he said: "In former days, charged with a mission, I was able to speak my heart in sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: " Then, with a mournful air, he said, "In former days, on a diplomatic mission, I was able to speak my heart to him in sincerity.

sentences.zh: 」彥詢所贈總詩，今見載《總集》。

translations.literal: " The poem Yanxun gave Zong is now found recorded in Zong's collected works.
translations.idiomatic: " The poem Yanxun gave Zong is now preserved in Zong's collected works.

sentences.zh: 彥謙早孤，不識父，為母兄鞠養。

translations.literal: Yanqian was orphaned early, never knew his father, and was reared by his elder brother through their mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanqian lost his father young and was raised by his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 長兄彥詢，雅有清鑒，以彥謙天性穎悟，每奇之，親教讀書。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yanxun had refined discernment; seeing Yanqian's natural quickness of understanding, he always marveled at him and personally taught him to read.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yanxun was a man of fine judgment; struck by Yanqian's native brilliance, he took a special interest in him and taught him himself.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，誦數萬言，為宗黨所異。

translations.literal: At age seven he could recite tens of thousands of words and was regarded as extraordinary by the clan and neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could recite tens of thousands of characters, and his kinfolk marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 十五出後叔父子貞，事所繼有逾本生。

translations.literal: At fifteen he was given in adoption to his uncle's son Zizhen and served his adoptive family with devotion exceeding that owed to his birth family.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he passed to his uncle's son Zizhen in adoption and showed his adoptive family a devotion beyond what he owed his birth kin.

sentences.zh: 子貞哀之，撫養甚厚。

translations.literal: Zizhen pitied him and raised him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen took pity on him and raised him with exceptional care.

sentences.zh: 後丁繼母憂，勺飲不入口者五日。

translations.literal: Later, upon the death of his stepmother, he took no spoonful or drink for five days.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died he went five days without food or water.

sentences.zh: 事伯父豹，竭盡心力，每四時珍果，弗敢先嘗。

translations.literal: In serving his uncle Bao he exhausted his heart and strength; whenever seasonal delicacies and fruits arrived, he dared not taste them first.
translations.idiomatic: He served his uncle Bao with every ounce of devotion and never tasted the season's first fruits before him.

sentences.zh: 遇期功之戚，必蔬食終禮，宗從取則焉。

translations.literal: When mourning kin of the qi and gong grades of mourning, he invariably ate vegetarian food until the rites were complete; the clan and kindred took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: For kin within the circle of formal mourning he kept to plain food until the rites were done, and the clan took him as their standard.

sentences.zh: 其後受學于博士尹琳，手不釋卷，遂通涉《五經》。

translations.literal: Thereafter he studied under the Erudite Yin Lin, never setting his scroll aside, and came to attain wide mastery of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied under Erudite Yin Lin, book ever in hand, until he had gained a thorough command of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 解屬文，雅有詞辯，風概高人。

translations.literal: He was skilled in literary composition, had refined eloquence in debate, and his bearing and spirit surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well, argued gracefully, and carried himself with a dignity that set him apart.

sentences.zh: 年十八，屬齊廣甯王孝珩為齊州刺史，辟為主簿。

translations.literal: At age eighteen, when Prince Guangning of Qi, Xiaohang, was made Inspector of Qizhou, Yanqian was summoned as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen, when Prince Guangning Xiaohang became Inspector of Qizhou, Yanqian was recruited as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時禁網疏闊，州郡之職，尤多縱弛。

translations.literal: At the time the prohibition net was loose and broad, and the duties of provinces and commanderies were especially slack and lax.
translations.idiomatic: The law was loosely enforced then, and provincial offices were especially undisciplined.

sentences.zh: 及彥謙在職，清簡守法，州境肅然，莫不敬憚。

translations.literal: When Yanqian held office, he was pure and simple and upheld the law; within the province all was orderly, and none failed to respect and fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yanqian the office grew austere and lawful; the province settled into order, and everyone held him in wary respect.

sentences.zh: 及周師入鄴，齊主東奔，以彥謙為齊州中從事。

translations.literal: When Zhou armies entered Ye, the Qi ruler fled east, and Yanqian was made Attendant of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Zhou forces entered Ye and the Qi ruler fled east, Yanqian was appointed Attendant of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 彥謙痛本朝傾覆，將糾率忠義，潛謀匡輔，事不果而止。

translations.literal: Yanqian grieved that his dynasty had collapsed; he intended to gather the loyal and righteous and secretly plotted to restore and assist the throne, but the affair did not succeed and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Heartbroken at his dynasty's fall, Yanqian tried to rally loyal men in a secret plot to restore the state, but the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，歸於家。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he went home.

sentences.zh: 周武帝遣柱國辛遵為齊州刺史，為賊帥輔帶劍所執。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou sent the Pillar of State Xin Zun as Inspector of Qizhou, and he was seized by the bandit chief Fu Daijian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou dispatched Pillar of State Xin Zun as Inspector of Qizhou, but the bandit leader Fu Daijian captured him.

sentences.zh: 彥謙以書諭之，帶劍慚懼，送遵還州，諸賊並各歸首。

translations.literal: Yanqian sent a letter instructing Daijian; ashamed and fearful, Daijian sent Zun back to the province, and all the bandits likewise surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqian wrote to reason with Daijian, who, shamed and afraid, sent Zun back; the other bandits surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 及隋文受禪之後，遂優遊鄉曲，誓無仕心。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the abdication, he then wandered at ease in his home district and swore he had no mind to serve in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Yanqian lived at ease in his native place and vowed never to serve again.

sentences.zh: 開皇七年，刺史韋藝固薦之，不得已而應命。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaihuang, Inspector Wei Yi repeatedly recommended him; unable to refuse, he answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaihuang, Inspector Wei Yi pressed his recommendation until Yanqian, left no choice, accepted appointment.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書盧愷一見重之，擢授承奉郎，俄遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Lu Kai honored him at first sight, promoted him to Gentleman of Presentation, and soon transferred him to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Lu Kai took to him immediately, appointed him Gentleman of Presentation, and soon made him an Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 後屬陳平，奉詔安撫泉、括等十州。

translations.literal: Later, when Chen was pacified, he received an edict to soothe and settle ten provinces including Quan and Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was conquered he was ordered to pacify ten provinces including Quan and Kuo.

sentences.zh: 以銜命稱旨，賜物百段、米百石、衣一襲、奴婢七口。

translations.literal: Because he carried out the commission in accord with the emperor's intent, he was granted a hundred bolts of goods, a hundred shi of rice, one suit of clothing, and seven household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: His mission pleased the throne, and he was rewarded with a hundred bolts of silk, a hundred shi of grain, a suit of clothes, and seven slaves.

sentences.zh: 遷秦州總管錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Recording Secretary of the Qinzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to recording secretary under the Qinzhou area command.

sentences.zh: 因朝集時，左僕射高熲定考課。

translations.literal: During the court assembly season, Left Vice Director Gao Yong was setting the performance evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: At the annual court assembly, Left Vice Director Gao Yong was conducting performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 彥謙謂熲曰：「《書》稱三載考績，黜陟幽明。

translations.literal: Yanqian said to Yong: "The Book of Documents says: 'Every three years examine merit and demote the obscure and promote the clear.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanqian said to Gao Yong, "The Book of Documents says, 'Every three years examine merit, demote the obscure, and promote the clear.'

sentences.zh: 唐、虞以降，代有其法，黜陟合理，褒貶無虧，便是進必得賢，退皆不肖。

translations.literal: From Tang and Yu downward, each age has had its method; when demotion and promotion are reasonable and praise and blame without loss, then advancement always gains the worthy and retirement removes the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of Tang and Yu onward, every dynasty has had its method; when promotion and demotion are just and praise and blame are honest, the worthy rise and the unworthy fall.

sentences.zh: 如或舛謬，法乃虛設。

translations.literal: If there are errors, the law becomes an empty formality.
translations.idiomatic: When the process goes wrong, the law becomes a hollow formality.

sentences.zh: 比見諸州考校，執見不同，進退多少，參差不類。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen the provincial evaluations: the views held differ, the numbers advanced and retired vary, and the results are irregular and inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have watched the provincial reviews: standards differ, the numbers promoted and dismissed vary wildly, and the results are a jumble.

sentences.zh: 況復愛憎肆意，致乖平坦。

translations.literal: Moreover, fondness and hatred are indulged at will, causing departure from fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, personal likes and dislikes run free and fairness is lost.

sentences.zh: 清介孤直，未必高第；

translations.literal: The pure, unyielding, and upright do not necessarily receive high grades;
translations.idiomatic: Men who are upright, austere, and uncompromising do not necessarily receive top marks;

sentences.zh: 卑諂巧官，翻居上等。

translations.literal: the base, flattering, and crafty officials instead rank at the top.
translations.idiomatic: while the servile and cunning often rank at the top.

sentences.zh: 真偽混淆，是非瞀亂。

translations.literal: Truth and falsehood are confused, and right and wrong are dimmed and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Truth and falsehood blur together and right and wrong are thrown into confusion.

sentences.zh: 宰貴既不精練，斟酌取捨，曾經驅使者，多以蒙識獲成；

translations.literal: The chief officials are neither well versed nor skilled; in their deliberations on selection and rejection, those previously dispatched on missions mostly pass evaluation through personal recognition;
translations.idiomatic: Because the reviewing officials are neither thorough nor skilled, those previously sent on missions mostly pass by personal acquaintance;

sentences.zh: 未曆台省者，皆為不知被退。

translations.literal: those who have never served in the secretariat or ministries are all dismissed as incompetent.
translations.idiomatic: while those who have never served at court are dismissed as unknown and incompetent.

sentences.zh: 又四方懸遠，難可詳悉，唯准量人數，半破半成。

translations.literal: Moreover, the four directions are distant and far-flung and hard to know in detail; they rely only on tallying head counts, half failing and half passing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the realm is vast and distant posts hard to know in detail, so reviewers simply count heads and fail half while passing half.

sentences.zh: 徒計官員之少多，莫顧善惡之眾寡。

translations.literal: They merely count how many officials there are, without regard to how many are good or bad.
translations.idiomatic: They tally only how many officials there are, never how many are good or bad.

sentences.zh: 俗求允當，其道無由。

translations.literal: In popular expectation of fairness, there is no way to achieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Under such conditions there is no path to the fairness people expect.

sentences.zh: 明公鑒達幽微，平心遇物，今年考校，必無阿枉，脫有前件數事，未審何以裁之？

translations.literal: You, my lord, perceive what is hidden and subtle and meet matters with an even heart; this year's evaluation will surely be free of partiality and distortion—yet if the aforesaid matters occur, I wonder by what standard you will judge them?
translations.idiomatic: You, my lord, see what is hidden and meet matters with an even heart; this year's review will surely be free of favor and distortion—yet if these abuses occur, by what standard will you judge them?

sentences.zh: 唯顧遠布耳目，精加採訪。

translations.literal: I only ask that you extend your hearing far and wide and carefully gather and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only that you extend your hearing far and wide and investigate with care.

sentences.zh: 褒秋毫之善，貶纖介之惡。

translations.literal: Praise goodness however slight; condemn evil however minute.
translations.idiomatic: Praise the slightest good and condemn the smallest wrong.

sentences.zh: 非直有光至道，亦足標獎賢能。

translations.literal: This would not only honor the supreme Way but also suffice to mark out and reward talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: That would not only honor the supreme Way but also mark out and reward true talent.

sentences.zh: 」詞氣侃然，觀者屬目。

translations.literal: " His words were bold and forthright, and those watching fixed their eyes upon him.
translations.idiomatic: " He spoke with bold forthrightness, and every eye in the hall turned to him.

sentences.zh: 熲為之動容，深見嗟賞。

translations.literal: Yong was moved by this and deeply expressed admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yong was visibly moved and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 因曆問河西、隴右官人景行，彥謙對之如響。

translations.literal: Thereupon he questioned in succession the conduct of officials west of the river and in Longyou, and Yanqian answered like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yong then quizzed him on the records of officials west of the river and in Longyou, and Yanqian answered without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 熲謂諸州總管、刺史曰：「與公言，不如獨共秦州考使語。

translations.literal: Yong said to the area commanders and inspectors of the provinces: "Talking with you gentlemen is not equal to speaking alone with the Qinzhou evaluation envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yong said to the area commanders and provincial inspectors, "Talking with you gentlemen is not worth speaking alone with the Qinzhou evaluation envoy.

sentences.zh: 」後數日，熲言於帝，帝弗能用。

translations.literal: " Several days later Yong spoke to the emperor, but the emperor could not employ Yanqian's recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: " Several days later Gao Yong reported to the emperor, but the throne did not act on Yanqian's advice.

sentences.zh: 以秩滿，遷長葛縣令，甚有惠化，百姓號為慈父。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was transferred to Magistrate of Changge County; he had very benevolent civilizing rule, and the common people called him the Merciful Father.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term he was made magistrate of Changge, where he governed with such kindness that the people called him the Merciful Father.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，帝令持節使者巡行州縣，察長吏能不。

translations.literal: During Renshou, the emperor ordered envoys bearing credentials to tour the provinces and counties and inspect whether the chief officials were capable or not.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign the emperor sent credentialed inspectors to tour the provinces and judge the competence of chief officials.

sentences.zh: 以彥謙為天下第一，超授鄀州司馬。

translations.literal: Yanqian was ranked first in all the realm and was specially promoted to Vice Governor of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanqian was rated the finest in the empire and was specially promoted to vice governor of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 吏人號哭相謂曰：「房明府今去，吾屬何用生為！

translations.literal: Officials and people wept and said to one another: "Magistrate Fang is leaving now—what use is there in our living!
translations.idiomatic: Officials and common people wept and said to one another, "Magistrate Fang is leaving—what use is there in our living!

sentences.zh: 」其後百姓思之，立碑頌德。

translations.literal: " Thereafter the common people missed him and erected a stele to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " Afterward the people missed him and erected a stele to praise his virtue.

sentences.zh: 鄀州久無刺史，州務皆歸彥謙，名有異政。

translations.literal: Ezhou long had no governor; provincial affairs all fell to Yanqian, and his reputation was for exceptional governance.
translations.idiomatic: Ezhou had gone without a governor for some time, and all provincial affairs devolved upon Yan Yanqian, whose reputation was for outstanding administration.

sentences.zh: 內史侍郎薛道衡，一代文宗，位望清顯。

translations.literal: Xue Daoheng, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was a literary patriarch of his generation, his position and repute clear and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daoheng, vice director of the Secretariat, was the leading literary figure of his age, eminent in rank and reputation.

sentences.zh: 所與交結，皆海內名賢。

translations.literal: Those with whom he formed ties were all renowned worthies within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: All his associates were famed men of talent throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 重彥謙為人，深加友敬。

translations.literal: He esteemed Yanqian as a man and deeply extended friendship and respect.
translations.idiomatic: He held Yan Yanqian in the highest regard and treated him with deep friendship and respect.

sentences.zh: 及為襄州總管，辭翰往來，交錯道路。

translations.literal: When he became Area Commander of Xiangzhou, letters and compositions passed back and forth, crisscrossing the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became area commander of Xiangzhou, their letters and poems crossed constantly on the roads between them.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，道衡轉牧番州，路經彥謙所，留連數日，屑涕而別。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded the throne, Daoheng was transferred to govern Fanzhou; passing by Yanqian's place on the road, he lingered several days and parted with tears streaming down his face.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Daoheng was transferred to govern Fan Prefecture; passing Yan Yanqian's home en route, he lingered for days and parted with tears streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎張衡亦與彥謙相善。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng, Attendant of the Yellow Gate, was also on good terms with Yanqian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng, attendant of the Yellow Gate, was also on friendly terms with Yan Yanqian.

sentences.zh: 于時帝營東都，窮極侈麗，天下失望。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor built the Eastern Capital, exhausting luxury and splendor, and all under Heaven were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor raised the Eastern Capital to the utmost luxury, and the realm lost hope in him.

sentences.zh: 又漢王構逆，罹罪者多。

translations.literal: Moreover the Prince of Han plotted rebellion, and many suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Prince of Han rose in rebellion, and many were punished.

sentences.zh: 彥謙見衡當塗而不能匡救，書諭之曰：

translations.literal: Yanqian saw that Heng stood at the helm of power yet could not remedy and save matters, and wrote to instruct him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Zhang Heng held power at court yet could not set things right, Yan Yanqian wrote to admonish him, saying:

sentences.zh: 竊聞賞者所以勸善，刑者所以懲惡。

translations.literal: I have privately heard that rewards are the means by which to encourage good, and punishments the means by which to chastise evil.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said that rewards exist to encourage good and punishments to chastise evil.

sentences.zh: 故疏賤之人，有善必賞；

translations.literal: Therefore for persons remote and base, if they have goodness they must be rewarded;
translations.idiomatic: So when the humble and lowly do good, they must be rewarded;

sentences.zh: 尊賢之戚，犯惡必刑。

translations.literal: for noble and worthy kin, if they commit evil they must be punished.
translations.idiomatic: and when kinsmen of the noble and worthy do wrong, they must be punished.

sentences.zh: 未有罰則避親，賞則遺賤者也。

translations.literal: There never was one who in punishing avoided kin and in rewarding omitted the base.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has justice meant sparing kin in punishment or forgetting the lowly in reward.

sentences.zh: 今國家祗承靈命，作人父母，刑賞曲直，升聞於天，夤畏照臨，亦宜謹肅。

translations.literal: Now the state reverently receives the numinous mandate, acting as father and mother to the people; the crookedness and straightness of punishments and rewards ascend and are heard in Heaven—deeply in awe of its shining oversight, one ought also to be careful and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: The state now reverently bears the sacred mandate and serves as father and mother to the people; the justice of punishments and rewards is heard in Heaven, and under that awesome gaze one ought to be scrupulous and solemn.

sentences.zh: 故文王云：「我其夙夜畏天之威。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wen said: "I shall early and late fear Heaven's awesomeness.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen therefore said, "I shall early and late stand in awe of Heaven's might.

sentences.zh: 」以此而論，雖州、國有殊，高下懸邈，憂人慎法，其理一也。

translations.literal: " Judging by this, though province and state differ and high and low are far apart, caring for people and revering law—the principle is one.
translations.idiomatic: " By this standard, though province and state differ and high and low stand far apart, the principle of caring for people and revering law is the same.

sentences.zh: 至如并州釁逆，須有甄明。

translations.literal: As for the rebellion at Bingzhou, there must be clear discrimination.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rebellion at Bingzhou, the facts must be clearly sorted out.

sentences.zh: 若楊諒實以詔命不通，慮宗社危逼，徵兵聚眾，非為幹紀，則當原其本情，議其刑罰；

translations.literal: If Yang Liang truly because edicts and orders did not reach him, fearing the altars of state were in peril, raised troops and gathered masses, not in order to violate law, then one ought to pardon his original intent and deliberate on his punishment;
translations.idiomatic: If Yang Liang truly raised troops because imperial orders never reached him and he feared for the altars of state—not to violate the law—then his original intent should be weighed and his punishment carefully considered;

sentences.zh: 上副聖主友于之意，下曉愚人疑惑之心。

translations.literal: above matching the sage lord's fraternal intent, below clarifying the confused hearts of foolish men.
translations.idiomatic: That would answer the emperor's brotherly intent above and settle the doubts of common men below.

sentences.zh: 若審知外內無虞，嗣後纂統，而好亂樂禍，妄有覬覦，則管、蔡之誅，當在於諒。

translations.literal: If it is truly known that within and without there was no worry, that after succession he would inherit the rule, yet he delighted in chaos and rejoiced in disaster and rashly harbored covetous designs, then the punishment of Guan and Cai ought to fall upon Liang.
translations.idiomatic: If it is clear that inside and outside the realm there was no threat, that succession was secure, yet he delighted in chaos and rashly coveted the throne, then the fate of Guan and Cai should be Yang Liang's.

sentences.zh: 同惡相濟，無所逃罪；

translations.literal: Those who share evil aid one another—nowhere to escape guilt;
translations.idiomatic: Accomplices who aid one another cannot escape guilt;

sentences.zh: 梟縣孥戮，國有常刑。

translations.literal: displaying heads and punishing wives and children—the state has fixed punishments.
translations.idiomatic: decapitation, public display, and punishment of wives and children—the state has fixed penalties for such crimes.

sentences.zh: 遂使籍沒流移，恐為冤濫。

translations.literal: Yet it has caused confiscation of registers and dispersal in exile—I fear this becomes wrongful excess.
translations.idiomatic: Yet families have been dispossessed and sent into exile—I fear this has become wrongful excess.

sentences.zh: 恢恢天網，豈其然乎！

translations.literal: The vast net of Heaven—could it really be so!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's vast net—surely it cannot be so!

sentences.zh: 罪疑從輕，斯義安在！

translations.literal: When guilt is doubtful, follow the lighter—where is this principle!
translations.idiomatic: When guilt is uncertain, leniency should prevail—where is that principle now!

sentences.zh: 昔叔向置鬻獄之死，晉國所嘉；

translations.literal: Of old Shu Xiang imposed death on the bribe-selling jailer, and the state of Jin commended it;
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu Xiang had a bribe-taking jailer put to death, and Jin praised him for it;

sentences.zh: 釋之斷犯蹕之刑，漢文稱善。

translations.literal: Zhang Shizhi cut short the punishment for violating the imperial procession, and Emperor Wen of Han praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizhi reduced the sentence for a breach of the imperial procession, and Emperor Wen praised his judgment.

sentences.zh: 羊舌甯不愛弟，廷尉非苟違君，俱以執法無私，不容輕重。

translations.literal: Yangshe Ning did not spare his younger brother, and the Commandant of Justice did not casually disobey his lord—both because in enforcing law they were without partiality and would not allow weight according to persons.
translations.idiomatic: Yangshe Ning did not spare his own brother, and the commandant of justice did not casually defy his sovereign—both enforced the law without favor and made no allowance for rank or connection.

sentences.zh: 且聖人大寶，是曰神器，苟非天命，不可妄得。

translations.literal: Moreover the sage's great treasure is called the divine vessel; if it is not the Mandate of Heaven, it cannot be rashly obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The throne is the sage's great treasure, the divine vessel—without Heaven's mandate it cannot be seized at will.

sentences.zh: 故蚩尤、項籍之驍勇，伊尹、霍光之權勢，李老、孔丘之才智，呂望、孫武之兵術，吳、楚連磐石之據，產、祿承母弟之基，不應曆運之兆，終無帝主之位。

translations.literal: Therefore the martial valor of Chiyou and Xiang Ji, the power and influence of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, the wisdom and talent of Laozi and Confucius, the military arts of Lü Wang and Sun Wu, the contiguous bedrock holdings of Wu and Chu, Chan and Lu inheriting the foundation of mother's younger brother—none responded to the portents of the succession cycle, and in the end had no position of emperor or lord.
translations.idiomatic: Chiyou and Xiang Yu were matchless in valor; Yi Yin and Huo Guang wielded supreme power; Laozi and Confucius possessed supreme wisdom; Lü Wang and Sun Wu mastered the art of war; Wu and Chu held territory firm as bedrock; Lü Chan and Lü Lu inherited a usurper's foundation—none matched the signs of destiny, and none ever gained the throne.

sentences.zh: 況乎蕞爾一隅，蜂扇蟻聚，楊諒之愚鄙，群小之凶慝，而欲憑陵畿甸，覬幸非望者哉。

translations.literal: How much less a tiny corner, bees fanning and ants gathering—the stupidity and baseness of Yang Liang, the vicious evil of petty men—and yet wishing to rely on force against the capital precinct and covet extraordinary fortune!
translations.idiomatic: How much less could a petty corner, a swarm of bees and ants—the foolish Yang Liang and his vicious underlings—hope to storm the capital and grasp at the throne!

sentences.zh: 開闢以降，書契雲及，帝皇之跡，可得而詳。

translations.literal: From the opening of the age down, written tallies cloud and reach; the traces of emperors and sovereigns can be obtained and known in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the world, written records abound, and the deeds of emperors can be studied in full.

sentences.zh: 自非積德累仁，豐功厚利，孰能道洽幽顯，義感靈祗？

translations.literal: Unless one accumulates virtue and amasses benevolence, with abundant merit and excellent benefit—who could harmonize the Way with what is hidden and manifest, and move spirit and gods with righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Who but those of accumulated virtue, abundant merit, and lasting benefit could unite the Way in this world and the next and move heaven itself with righteousness?

sentences.zh: 是以古之哲王，昧旦丕顯，履冰在念，禦朽兢懷。

translations.literal: Therefore the wise kings of old, at dark dawn made great their brightness, treading ice in thought, repairing rot with anxious care.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the wise kings of old rose before dawn to govern, ever mindful as if treading on ice, ever anxious as if mending a roof before it collapses.

sentences.zh: 逮叔世驕荒，曾無戒懼，肆於人上，騁嗜奔欲，不司具載，謂略陳之。

translations.literal: But reaching the later age of pride and debauchery, there was never caution or fear; indulging above men, galloping in appetites and rushing after desires—not all can be fully set forth; I say I shall briefly present them.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages grew proud and reckless and never took warning; rulers indulged every appetite from their thrones—too many examples to recount here, so I shall mention only a few.

sentences.zh: 曩者，齊、陳二國，並居大位。

translations.literal: Formerly the two states of Qi and Chen both occupied the great throne.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Qi and Chen both occupied thrones.

sentences.zh: 自謂與天地合德，日月齊明，罔念憂虞，不恤刑政。

translations.literal: They deemed themselves in virtue aligned with Heaven and Earth, in brightness equal to sun and moon, without thought of worry and care, not pitying punishments and government.
translations.idiomatic: Each ruler imagined his virtue matched Heaven and Earth and his brilliance equaled the sun and moon, never heeding danger and neglecting law and governance.

sentences.zh: 近臣懷寵，稱善而隱惡；

translations.literal: Close ministers cherished favor, praising good and hiding evil;
translations.idiomatic: Favored courtiers praised every good deed and hid every fault;

sentences.zh: 史官曲筆，掩瑕而錄美。

translations.literal: historians bent their brushes, covering flaws and recording beauty.
translations.idiomatic: historians bent their brushes, concealing flaws and recording only virtues.

sentences.zh: 是以人庶呼嗟，終閉塞於視聽；

translations.literal: Therefore the common people sighed and lamented, yet in the end were blocked from sight and hearing;
translations.idiomatic: The common people groaned in misery yet remained shut out from the ruler's eyes and ears;

sentences.zh: 公卿虛譽，日敷陳於左右。

translations.literal: dukes and ministers offered empty praise, daily set forth at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: while high officials daily filled the throne's ears with empty praise.

sentences.zh: 法網嚴密，刑辟日多，賦役煩興，老幼疲苦。

translations.literal: The law's net was strict and dense, punishments daily increased, levies and corvée wearisomely arose, old and young exhausted in bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: The law grew ever tighter, punishments multiplied, levies and corvée multiplied, and old and young alike were worn to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 昔鄭有子產，齊有晏嬰，楚有叔敖，晉有士會，凡此小國，尚足名臣，齊、陳之強，豈無良佐？

translations.literal: Of old Zheng had Zichan, Qi had Yan Ying, Chu had Shu Ao, Jin had Shi Hui—as for all these small states, they still had famed ministers; Qi and Chen in their strength—could they have lacked good assistants?
translations.idiomatic: Once Zheng had Zichan, Qi had Yan Ying, Chu had Sunshu Ao, and Jin had Shi Hui—even small states could boast great ministers; could mighty Qi and Chen have lacked worthy counselors?

sentences.zh: 但以執政壅蔽，懷私殉軀，忘國憂家，外同內忌。

translations.literal: It was only that those holding power blocked and blinded, cherishing private ends and sacrificing their bodies, forgetting the state and worrying only for family, outwardly harmonious yet inwardly jealous.
translations.idiomatic: But those in power blinded their rulers, sacrificed the state for personal gain, forgot the country's needs in family quarrels, and pretended unity while scheming against one another.

sentences.zh: 設有正直之士，才堪幹時，於己非宜，即加擯棄；

translations.literal: Suppose there were upright men whose talent suited the times—if unsuitable to oneself, they were at once rejected and cast aside;
translations.idiomatic: When an upright man of real talent appeared, if he did not suit their interests they cast him aside;

sentences.zh: 儻遇諂佞之輩，行多穢慝，于我有益，遽蒙薦舉。

translations.literal: if perchance one met fawning flatterers whose conduct was mostly foul and wicked—if beneficial to oneself, they were promptly recommended and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: when a flattering scoundrel whose conduct was vile but useful to them appeared, he was promptly promoted.

sentences.zh: 以此求賢，何從而至。

translations.literal: With this to seek worthies—from what path would they come?
translations.idiomatic: How could true talent ever be found that way?

sentences.zh: 夫賢材者，非尚膂力，豈系文華，唯須正身負戴。

translations.literal: As for men of talent, it is not that physical strength is honored, nor that literary polish is the tie—one need only have upright bodies bearing the load.
translations.idiomatic: True talent is not a matter of muscle or literary polish; what matters is an upright person who can bear the weight of office.

sentences.zh: 確乎不動，譬棟之處屋，如骨之在身，所謂棟樑骨鯁之材也。

translations.literal: Firm and unmoving, like a ridgepole placed in a house, like bone in the body—what is called timber of ridgepole and spine.
translations.idiomatic: Firm and unmoving, like a ridgepole in a roof or bone in the body—this is what is meant by pillar-and-backbone timber.

sentences.zh: 齊、陳不任骨鯁，信近讒諛，天高聽卑，監其淫僻。

translations.literal: Qi and Chen did not employ backbone talent, trusted and drew near slanderers and flatterers—Heaven is high yet hears what is low, overseeing their debauchery and perversity.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Chen refused such backbone men, trusted slanderers and flatterers instead—and Heaven, though high, hears what is below, and watched their debauchery.

sentences.zh: 故總收神器，歸我大隋。

translations.literal: Therefore they altogether gathered the divine vessel, returning it to our Great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: And so the imperial throne was gathered in and came to our Great Sui.

sentences.zh: 向使二國祗敬上玄，惠恤鰥寡，委任方直，斥遠浮華，卑菲為心，惻隱是務，河朔強富，江湖險隔，各保其業，人不思亂，泰山之固，弗可動也。

translations.literal: If formerly the two states reverently honored the Supreme Mystery, showed kindness to widowers and widows, entrusted office to the upright, repelled and kept distant empty show, took lowliness and thrift as heart, made pity their task—though the north of the river was strong and rich and rivers and lakes were perilously divided, each would preserve its estate, people would not think of chaos, and Mount Tai's solidity could not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Had both states reverently served Heaven, cared for the helpless, entrusted power to upright men, driven off the ostentatious, embraced humility and compassion—though the north were strong and the south divided by rivers and lakes, each realm would have kept its place, the people would not have dreamed of rebellion, and their thrones would have stood firm as Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 然而寢臥積薪，宴安鴆毒，遂使禾黍生廟，務露沾衣，吊影撫心，何嗟及矣！

translations.literal: Yet they slept atop piled kindling, feasted in ease and drank poison—so that millet grew in the ancestral temple, dew of affairs soaked their robes; mourning their shadows and clutching their hearts—what sigh could reach it!
translations.idiomatic: Instead they slept on kindling and drank poison in false peace until millet grew in their ancestral temples and dew soaked their robes in exile—clutching their hearts alone in misery, what use was regret then!

sentences.zh: 故《詩》云：「殷之未喪師，克配上帝。

translations.literal: Therefore the Book of Odes says: "Before Yin had not yet lost its armies, it could match the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes therefore says, "Before Yin lost its armies, it could match God on high.

sentences.zh: 宜鑒於殷，駿命不易。

translations.literal: One ought to take Yin as mirror—the swift mandate is not easily changed.
translations.idiomatic: Take Yin as your mirror—the mandate is not easily kept.

sentences.zh: 」萬機之事，何者不須熟慮哉。

translations.literal: " Of the myriad affairs of state, which does not require mature deliberation!
translations.idiomatic: " Which affair of state does not require the deepest deliberation?

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝望雲就日，仁孝夙彰，錫社分珪，大成規矩。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, gazing at clouds and approaching the sun, benevolence and filial piety long made manifest, granted fiefs and divided jade scepters, greatly completed rules and measures.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, like one who turns toward clouds and sun, has long shown benevolence and filial piety; enfeoffed and granted jade, you have fully established the norms of rule.

sentences.zh: 及總統淮海，盛德日新，當璧之符，遐邇僉屬。

translations.literal: When you overall governed Huai and Hai, your splendid virtue daily renewed, the tally of jade accorded—far and near all joined in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When you governed the Huai-Hai region your virtue grew daily brighter, and the mandate of the jade tally was acclaimed far and near.

sentences.zh: 纘曆甫爾，寬仁已布，率土蒼生，翹足而喜。
