translations.literal: Having just inherited the calendar, lenience and benevolence were already spread; all the land's living folk stood on tiptoe in joy.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had you ascended the throne when mercy and kindness were proclaimed, and all the people rejoiced in expectation.

sentences.zh: 并州之亂，變起倉卒，職由楊諒詭惑，詿誤吏人；

translations.literal: The disorder at Bingzhou arose in sudden haste; its source lay in Yang Liang's deceit and confusion, misleading officials and people;
translations.idiomatic: The Bingzhou revolt erupted suddenly, stirred by Yang Liang's deception and the misleading of officials and people;

sentences.zh: 非有構怨本朝，棄德從賊者也。

translations.literal: there were none who harbored grudges against the dynasty or abandoned virtue to follow rebels.
translations.idiomatic: not because they bore grievances against the dynasty or chose rebellion over loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而有司將帥，稱其願反，非止誣陷良善，亦恐大玷皇猷。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible officials and generals call them willing to rebel—this not only falsely traps the good, but also I fear greatly stains the imperial design.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials and generals call them willing rebels—this not only falsely condemns the innocent but may grievously stain your imperial purpose.

sentences.zh: 足下宿當重寄，早預心膂，粵自籓邸，柱石見知，方當書名竹帛，傳芳萬古，稷、契、伊、呂，彼獨何人。

translations.literal: You, sir, long bore heavy trust, early entered the heart and sinew; from the princely residence you were known as pillar and stone—soon your name should be written on bamboo and silk, fragrance transmitted ten thousand ages—Ji, Qi, Yi, Lü—what sort of men were they alone?
translations.idiomatic: You have long borne heavy trust and been close to the throne's inner circle; known as a pillar since the princely years, your name is destined for the histories alongside Ji, Qi, Yi Yin, and Lü Wang—who were they, that you should not be?

sentences.zh: 既屬明時，須存謇諤，立當世之大誡，作將來之憲范，豈容曲順人主，以愛虧刑；

translations.literal: Since you belong to an enlightened age, you must preserve forthright remonstrance, establish the great admonition of the present age, and make the law and model for the future—how can you allow bending to suit the lord of men, through affection impairing punishments;
translations.idiomatic: In an enlightened age you must speak blunt truth, set a warning for the present and a standard for the future—how can you bend to the sovereign's feelings and weaken justice for affection's sake;

sentences.zh: 又使脅從之徒，橫貽罪譴。

translations.literal: and also cause those compelled to follow to suffer punishment without cause.
translations.idiomatic: or leave those who were forced to follow bearing punishment they do not deserve?

sentences.zh: 忝蒙眷遇，輒寫微誠，野人愚瞽，不知忌諱。

translations.literal: I am shamed to receive your gracious favor and rashly write my slight sincerity—a rustic man, foolish and blind, not knowing what is taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Graced as I am by your favor, I venture these honest thoughts—a rustic man, foolish and blind to what should not be said.

sentences.zh: 衡得書，歎息而不敢奏聞。

translations.literal: Heng received the letter, sighed, and did not dare report it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng received the letter, sighed deeply, and dared not report it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 彥謙知王綱不振，遂去官，隱居不仕。

translations.literal: Yanqian knew the royal net was not restored, then left office and lived in seclusion without serving.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanqian saw that imperial authority was failing, resigned his post, and withdrew into seclusion.

sentences.zh: 將結構蒙山之下，以求其志。

translations.literal: He was about to build a structure beneath Mount Meng to seek his aim.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to build a retreat beneath Mount Meng to pursue his ideals.

sentences.zh: 會置司隸官，盛選天下知名之士。

translations.literal: It happened that the office of Metropolitan Inspector was established, and famed men of the realm were grandly selected.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Metropolitan Inspectorate was established and the court sought out the most renowned men in the land.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以彥謙公方宿著，時望所歸，征授司隸刺史。

translations.literal: The court, because Yanqian's public rectitude was long renowned and the age's hopes converged upon him, summoned and appointed him Metropolitan Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The court, recognizing Yan Yanqian's long-standing integrity and the esteem in which he was held, summoned him as metropolitan inspector.

sentences.zh: 彥謙亦慨然有澄清天下之志，凡所薦舉，皆人倫表式。

translations.literal: Yanqian also resolutely had the ambition to clarify and purify all under Heaven; all whom he recommended were models among mankind.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanqian took up the post with a resolute will to cleanse the realm; every man he recommended was a model of moral worth.

sentences.zh: 其有彈射，當之者曾無怨言。

translations.literal: When he made impeachments, those who were targeted never had complaint in their words.
translations.idiomatic: Those he impeached never uttered a word of complaint.

sentences.zh: 司隸別駕劉灹陵上侮下，訐以為直，刺史憚之，皆為之拜。

translations.literal: Liu Ye, Vice Director of the Metropolitan Inspectorate, insulted those above and bullied those below, taking accusation as straightness; inspectors feared him and all bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye, a vice director of the Metropolitan Inspectorate, bullied his superiors and insulted his subordinates while posing as blunt honesty; provincial inspectors feared him and all bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 唯彥謙執志不撓，抗禮長揖。

translations.literal: Only Yanqian held to his intent unmoved, opposing with ceremony in a long bow.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yan Yanqian held firm, returning his greeting with an equal bow but no deference.

sentences.zh: 有識嘉之，

translations.literal: Men of discernment praised this,
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment praised him for it,

sentences.zh: 灹亦不恨。

translations.literal: and Ye also bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Ye bore no resentment.

sentences.zh: 大業九年，從駕度遼，監扶餘道軍事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye he followed the imperial carriage crossing Liaodong and supervised military affairs on the Fuyu route.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor on the Liaodong campaign and oversaw forces on the Fuyu route.

sentences.zh: 其後隋政漸亂，莫不變節，彥謙直道守常，頗為執政者所嫉。

translations.literal: Afterward as Sui government gradually fell into disorder, none failed to change their principles; Yanqian kept to the straight Way unchanged and was much envied by those holding power.
translations.idiomatic: As Sui politics grew chaotic, others all shifted with the times, but Yan Yanqian held to the straight path and was much resented by those in power.

sentences.zh: 出為涇陽令，終於官。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Magistrate of Jingyang and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to magistrate of Jingyang and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 彥謙居家，每子侄定省，常為講說督勉之，亹癖不倦。

translations.literal: When Yanqian was at home, whenever nephews and sons came on morning and evening visits, he always lectured and exhorted them, assiduously and without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: At home, whenever his sons and nephews came on their daily visits, he would instruct and encourage them tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 家有舊業，資產素殷，又前後居官所得俸祿，皆以周恤親友，家無餘財。

translations.literal: The family had hereditary estates and assets naturally abundant; moreover the salary from successive offices was all used to succor and comfort kin and friends—the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The family had inherited wealth, and every salary he earned in office went to help relatives and friends, leaving nothing behind.

sentences.zh: 車服器用，務存素儉。

translations.literal: Carriages, robes, vessels, and implements—he strove to keep them plain and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: His carriages, clothing, and household goods were kept plain and frugal.

sentences.zh: 自少及長，一言一行，未嘗涉私。

translations.literal: From youth to age, in every word and act he never involved private ends.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to age, not a word or deed of his ever served private ends.

sentences.zh: 雖致屢空，怡然自得。

translations.literal: Though his house was often empty, he was cheerful and content in himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though poverty often left his house bare, he remained cheerful and at ease.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容獨笑，顧謂其子玄齡曰：「人皆因祿富，我獨以官貧。

translations.literal: Once, composed and laughing alone, he turned and said to his son Xuanling: "Others all through salary grow rich; I alone through office am poor.
translations.idiomatic: Once, smiling quietly to himself, he turned to his son Xuanling and said, "Others grow rich from office; I alone have grown poor from it.

sentences.zh: 所遺子孫，在於清白耳。

translations.literal: What I leave to sons and grandsons lies only in integrity.
translations.idiomatic: All I leave my descendants is a name for integrity.

sentences.zh: 」所有文筆，恢廓閒雅，有古人之深致。

translations.literal: " His prose writings were vast, easy, and refined, with the ancients' deep resonances.
translations.idiomatic: " His prose was broad, easy, and refined, with the deep resonance of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 又善草隸，人有得其尺牘者，皆寶玩之。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at cursive and clerical script; those who obtained even a foot of his letters all treasured and enjoyed them.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script, and anyone who obtained even a letter of his treasured it.

sentences.zh: 太原王劭、北海高構、蓧縣李綱、中山郎茂、郎穎、河東柳彧、薛孺，皆一時知名雅澹之士，彥謙並與為友。

translations.literal: Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Gao Gou of Beihai, Li Gang of Diaoxian, Lang Mao and Lang Ying of Zhongshan, Liu Yu of Hedong, and Xue Ru—all famed, refined, and serene men of the time—Yanqian was friends with them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Gao Gou of Beihai, Li Gang of Diaoxian, Lang Mao and Lang Ying of Zhongshan, Liu Yu of Hedong, and Xue Ru were all celebrated men of refined character in their day, and Yan Yanqian counted them all as friends.

sentences.zh: 雖冠蓋成列，而門無雜賓。

translations.literal: Though official caps and covers formed rows, his gate had no mixed guests.
translations.idiomatic: Though officials called constantly, his door admitted no unworthy guest.

sentences.zh: 體資文雅，深達政務，有識者咸以遠大許之。

translations.literal: In person he was endowed with cultured refinement, deeply versed in affairs of government; men of discernment all credited him with far-reaching greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Refined in bearing and deeply versed in governance, discerning men all credited him with greatness yet to come.

sentences.zh: 初，開皇中平陳之後，天下一統，論者咸雲將致太平。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in Kaihuang after the pacification of Chen, all under Heaven was unified; commentators all said that great peace would arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, after the conquest of Chen in the Kaihuang era united the realm, many predicted an age of peace.

sentences.zh: 彥謙私謂所親趙郡李少通曰：「主上性多忌克，不納諫諍。

translations.literal: Yanqian privately said to his close associate Li Shaotong of Zhao Commandery: "Our lord by nature is much given to jealousy and conquest, and does not accept remonstrance and dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanqian confided to his friend Li Shaotong of Zhao Commandery, "The emperor is jealous by nature and will not hear remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 太子卑弱，諸王擅威。

translations.literal: The crown prince is weak and lowly; the princes monopolize authority.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is weak, and the princes wield power on their own.

sentences.zh: 在朝惟行苛酷之政，未弘遠大之體，天下雖安，方憂危亂。

translations.literal: At court they only carry out harsh and cruel policy, not spreading the great and far-reaching body of rule; though all under Heaven is at peace, I am now anxious about peril and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The court pursues only harsh policies and never the broader vision of rule; though the realm seems secure, I already foresee trouble ahead.

sentences.zh: 」少通初謂不然。

translations.literal: " At first Shaotong considered this not so.
translations.idiomatic: " At first Li Shaotong disagreed.

sentences.zh: 及仁壽、大業之際，其言皆驗。

translations.literal: When it reached the Renshou and Daye periods, his words were all verified.
translations.idiomatic: By the Renshou and Daye reigns, every word of his had come true.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，以子玄齡著勳庸，贈徐州都督、臨淄縣公，諡曰定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, because his son Xuanling achieved merit and service, he was posthumously given Regional Commander of Xuzhou and Duke of Linzi County, with posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign, because his son Fang Xuanling had earned great merit, he was posthumously made regional commander of Xuzhou and Duke of Linzi, with the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 伯祖弟幼湣，安豐、新蔡二郡太守，坐事奪官。

translations.literal: His uncle's younger brother Youmin had been Administrator of the two commanderies of Anfeng and Xincai; for an offense his office was removed.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle's younger brother Youmin had served as administrator of Anfeng and Xincai, but lost his post after an offense.

sentences.zh: 居家，忽聞門有客聲，出無所見，還至庭中，為家群犬所噬，卒。

translations.literal: While at home, he suddenly heard the sound of a guest at the door; going out he saw nothing; returning to the courtyard he was bitten by the household dogs and died.
translations.idiomatic: At home one day he suddenly heard what sounded like a visitor at the door. He went out and saw no one, but when he returned to the courtyard the family dogs set upon him and he died.

sentences.zh: 景伯字良暉，法壽族子也。

translations.literal: Jingbo, styled Lianghui, was a clansman of Fashou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jingbo, styled Lianghui, was a clansman of Fang Fashou.

sentences.zh: 祖元慶，仕宋。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanking served the Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fang Yuanking had served the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 曆七郡太守，後為沈文秀青州建威府司馬。

translations.literal: He served successively as Administrator of seven commanderies, and afterward became Chief Clerk of the Jianwei Headquarters of Qingzhou under Shen Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: He governed seven commanderies in succession and later became chief clerk on Shen Wenxiu's Jianwei staff in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝之殺廢帝子業，子業弟子勳起兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Song killed the deposed Emperor Ziye, Ziye's younger brother Zixun raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Song killed the deposed emperor Ziye, Ziye's younger brother Zixun took up arms.

sentences.zh: 文秀後歸子勳，元慶不同，為文秀所害。

translations.literal: Wenxiu afterward submitted to Zixun; Yuanking did not agree and was killed by Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu later joined Zixun's side, but Yuanking refused and was killed by Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 父愛親，獻文時，三齊平，隨例內徙，為平齊人。

translations.literal: His father Aiqin: in the time of Emperor Xianwen, when the Three Qi were pacified, was relocated inward according to precedent and became a Pingqi person.
translations.idiomatic: His father Aiqin, after the Three Qi were pacified in the reign of Emperor Xianwen, was relocated inland by the usual rule and registered as a Pingqi subject.

sentences.zh: 以父非命，疏服終身。

translations.literal: Because his father died by violence, he wore simple mourning garb for life.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died by violence, he wore simple mourning dress for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 景伯生於桑乾，少喪父，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jingbo was born at Sanggan; he lost his father young and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jingbo was born at Sanggan, lost his father young, and was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 家貧，傭書自給，養母甚謹。

translations.literal: The family was poor; he copied books to support himself and cared for his mother with great diligence.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, so he copied books for hire to support himself and cared for his mother with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 尚書盧陽烏稱之于李沖。

translations.literal: Minister of the Interior Lu Yangwu recommended him to Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yangwu of the Ministry of Interior recommended him to Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 沖時典選，拔為奉朝請。

translations.literal: Chong then held charge of selection and promoted him to Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong then oversaw appointments and selected him as Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 累遷齊州輔國長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the State in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to chief clerk on the Pacification of the State staff in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 會刺史亡，敕行州事。

translations.literal: When the Inspector happened to die, an edict ordered him to administer provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial inspector died, he was ordered by edict to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 政存寬簡，百姓安之。

translations.literal: His governance was marked by leniency and simplicity, and the common people found peace in it.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency and restraint, and the people were content.

sentences.zh: 後除清河太守。

translations.literal: Later he was made Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed administrator of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 郡人劉簡武曾失禮于景伯，聞其臨郡，闔家逃亡。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Liu Jianwu, had once been disrespectful toward Jingbo; when he heard Jingbo was coming to govern the commandery, his whole household fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianwu of the commandery had once offended Fang Jingbo; when he learned Jingbo was coming to govern the district, his whole family fled.

sentences.zh: 景伯督切屬縣，追捕禽之。

translations.literal: Jingbo urged the subordinate counties to press the search, pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo pressed the subordinate counties to hunt him down and had him captured.

sentences.zh: 即署其子為西曹掾，令喻山賊。

translations.literal: He immediately appointed the man's son as Western Bureau Assistant and ordered him to persuade the mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He at once appointed the man's son as western bureau assistant and sent him to persuade the mountain bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊以景伯不念舊惡，一時俱下，論者稱之。

translations.literal: The bandits, because Jingbo did not bear old grudges, all came down at once; commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jingbo bore no old grudge, the bandits all surrendered at once, and commentators praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 舊制，守令六年為限。

translations.literal: By the old regulation, prefects and magistrates had a limit of six years.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule, prefects and magistrates served a six-year term.

sentences.zh: 限滿將代，郡人韓靈和等三百餘人表訴乞留，復加二載。

translations.literal: When the term limit was full and he was about to be replaced, more than three hundred people of the commandery including Han Linghe submitted a petition begging that he remain, and he was given two more years.
translations.idiomatic: When his term was up and a successor was due, more than three hundred petitioners led by Han Linghe begged the court to keep him, and he was granted two more years.

sentences.zh: 後為司空長史，以母疾去官。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works, but left office because of his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief clerk to the Minister of Works but resigned when his mother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 景伯性復淳和。

translations.literal: Jingbo's nature was moreover pure and gentle.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jingbo was further noted for a gentle, upright character.

sentences.zh: 涉獵經史，諸弟宗之，如事嚴親。

translations.literal: He ranged through the classics and histories; the younger brothers revered him as they would a strict parent.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories, and his younger brothers revered him as they would a stern elder.

sentences.zh: 及弟亡，蔬食終喪，期不內禦，憂毀之容，有如居重。

translations.literal: When a younger brother died, he ate plain food through the mourning period, for a full year did not enter the inner quarters, and his grieving, wasted appearance was as though he bore heavy mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When a younger brother died, he ate only plain food through the mourning period, did not enter the inner quarters for a full year, and wore an expression of grief as deep as for a parent.

sentences.zh: 其次弟景先亡，其幼弟景遠期年哭臨，亦不內寢。

translations.literal: When his next younger brother Jingxian died, his youngest brother Jingyuan mourned and wept for a full year and likewise did not sleep in the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When his next younger brother Fang Jingxian died, his youngest brother Fang Jingyuan mourned for a full year and likewise slept outside the inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 鄉里為之語曰：「有義有禮，房家兄弟。

translations.literal: The local people made a saying: "Righteous and courteous, the Fang brothers.
translations.idiomatic: People in the district had a saying: "Righteous and courteous, the Fang brothers.

sentences.zh: 」廷尉卿崔光韶好標榜人物，無所推尚，每雲景伯有士大夫之行業。

translations.literal: " Grand Minister of Justice Cui Guangshao loved to hold up men for renown yet praised no one; he always said Jingbo had the conduct and achievement of a scholar-official.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Minister of Justice Cui Guangshao loved to pass judgment on men yet praised almost no one; he always said Fang Jingbo possessed the bearing and achievement of a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 及母亡，景伯居喪，不食鹽菜。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Jingbo observed mourning and ate neither salt nor vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Fang Jingbo went into mourning and took neither salt nor vegetables.

sentences.zh: 因此遂為水病，積年不愈。

translations.literal: Because of this he thereafter developed edema and for years did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: This brought on edema from which he suffered for years without recovery.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，贈左將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He died at home and was posthumously given General of the Left and Inspector of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home and was posthumously made General of the Left and inspector of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 景伯子文烈，位司徒左長史，與從父弟逸祐並有名。

translations.literal: Jingbo's son Wenlie held the post of Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister over the Masses, and together with his father's younger male cousin Yiyou both had fame.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo's son Fang Wenlie served as chief clerk of the left under the Minister over the Masses and, together with his father's younger cousin Yiyou, enjoyed wide renown.

sentences.zh: 文烈性溫柔，未嘗嗔怒。

translations.literal: Wenlie's nature was gentle and mild; he never showed anger.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Wenlie was gentle by nature and never grew angry.

sentences.zh: 為吏部郎時，經霖雨絕糧，遣婢糴米，因爾逃竄，三四日方還。

translations.literal: When he was Secretary of the Ministry of Personnel, prolonged rains cut off grain; he sent a maid to buy rice, and she thereupon fled and hid, returning only after three or four days.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, prolonged rains cut off their food supply. He sent a maid to buy rice, but she ran off and did not return for three or four days.

sentences.zh: 文烈徐謂曰：「舉家無食，汝何處來？

translations.literal: Wenlie said calmly to her: "The whole house has no food; where have you come from?
translations.idiomatic: Fang Wenlie said calmly to her, "The whole household has nothing to eat; where have you been?

sentences.zh: 」竟無捶撻。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not beat her.
translations.idiomatic: " He never raised a hand to punish her.

sentences.zh: 子山基，仕隋，曆戶部、考功侍郎，並著能名，見稱于時。

translations.literal: His son Shanji served the Sui and successively held the posts of Vice Minister of the Household and Vice Minister of Evaluating Merit, both with noted ability, and was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang Shanji served the Sui, held posts as vice minister in the ministries of revenue and evaluation, won renown for his ability, and was widely praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 景先字光胄，幼孤貧，無資從師，其母自授《毛詩》、《曲禮》。

translations.literal: Jingxian, styled Guangzhou, was orphaned and poor young; he had no means to follow a teacher, and his mother herself taught him the Mao Odes and the Ceremonial Records.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jingxian, styled Guangzhou, was orphaned and poor as a boy, could not afford a teacher, and was instructed at home by his mother in the Mao Odes and the Ceremonial Records.

sentences.zh: 年十二，請其母曰：「豈可使兄傭賃以供景先也？

translations.literal: At age twelve he asked his mother: "How can I let my elder brother hire himself out to support Jingxian?
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he said to his mother, "How can I let my elder brother hire himself out to support me?

sentences.zh: 請自求衣，然後就學。

translations.literal: Let me seek clothing for myself, and then go to study.
translations.idiomatic: Let me earn my own clothes, and then I will go to school.

sentences.zh: 」母哀其小，不許。

translations.literal: " His mother pitied his youth and did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " His mother, pitying his youth, refused.

sentences.zh: 苦請乃從之。

translations.literal: He pleaded persistently until she yielded.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded until she gave in.

sentences.zh: 遂得一羊裘，忻然自足。

translations.literal: Thereupon he obtained a sheepskin coat and was glad and content.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained a sheepskin coat and was perfectly content.

sentences.zh: 晝則樵蘇，夜誦經史，遂大通贍。

translations.literal: By day he gathered firewood and kindling; by night he recited the classics and histories, and thus attained wide mastery.
translations.idiomatic: By day he gathered firewood; by night he read the classics and histories until he had mastered them thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 太和中，例得還鄉，解褐太學博士。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, by precedent he was permitted to return to his home region and left office dress to become Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he was allowed to return home under the usual rule and took his first office as erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 時太常劉芳、侍中崔光當世儒宗，歎其精博，奏兼著作佐郎，修國史。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Commandant Liu Fang and Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang were the Confucian masters of the age; they praised his thorough mastery and memorialized that he also serve as Assistant Gentleman for Drafting, compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, grand commandant of the Ministry of Rites, and Cui Guang, attendant-in-ordinary, were the leading scholars of the age; impressed by Jingxian's breadth of learning, they memorialized that he also serve as assistant drafter and help compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 侍中穆紹又啟景先撰《宣武起居注》。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Mu Shao further memorialized that Jingxian compose the Daily Records of Emperor Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Mu Shao further recommended that Jingxian compile the Daily Records of Emperor Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 累遷步兵校尉，領尚書郎、齊州中正，所曆皆有當官稱。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Colonel of Foot Soldiers, concurrently holding the posts of Gentleman of the Interior and Primary Evaluator of Qizhou; in every post he fulfilled office worthily.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to colonel of foot soldiers while serving concurrently as a gentleman of the interior and primary evaluator of Qizhou, and in every post earned praise worthy of his rank.

sentences.zh: 景先沈敏方正，事兄恭謹，出告反面，晨昏參省，側立移時，兄亦危坐，相敬如賓。

translations.literal: Jingxian was deep, sharp, upright, and square in character; in serving his elder brother he was reverent and careful, going out he reported and returning he presented himself; morning and evening he paid respects; he stood at the side for long periods. The elder brother also sat upright, and they honored each other as guests.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jingxian was thoughtful, upright, and serious; toward his elder brother he was reverent and exact, reporting when he went out and presenting himself on return, attending morning and evening, standing respectfully for long stretches while his brother sat upright. They treated each other with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 兄曾寢疾，景先侍湯藥，衣冠不解，形容毀瘁。

translations.literal: When his elder brother once lay ill, Jingxian attended his broth and medicine, never removing cap and robes, his appearance wasted and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother fell ill, Jingxian nursed him night and day without removing cap or robes, until he was haggard with worry.

sentences.zh: 親友見者，莫不哀之。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends who saw this were all moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends who saw him were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 卒，特贈洛州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: When he died, he was specially posthumously given Inspector of Luozhou, with posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was specially made inspector of Luozhou posthumously, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 景先作《五經疑問》百餘篇，其語典該。

translations.literal: Jingxian composed more than a hundred chapters of Questions on the Five Classics; his language was canonical and complete.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jingxian wrote more than a hundred chapters of Questions on the Five Classics, written in a style both authoritative and thorough.

sentences.zh: 符璽郎王神貴益之，名為《辯疑》，合成十卷，亦有可觀。

translations.literal: Seal Officer Wang Shengui augmented it and named it Resolving Doubts; together they made ten scrolls, which also had merit worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shengui of the Office of Seals expanded the work and named it Resolving Doubts; the ten scrolls together make worthwhile reading.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝時，奏上之。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Jiemin it was submitted to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Jiemin it was submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝親自執卷，與神貴往復，嘉其用心。

translations.literal: The emperor personally held the scroll and exchanged views with Shengui, praising their earnest intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the scroll himself and discussed it back and forth with Shengui, praising their careful work.

sentences.zh: 子延祐，武定末太子家令，後隸魏收修史。

translations.literal: His son Yanyou, at the end of Wuding, was Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, and afterward joined Wei Shou in compiling history.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang Yanyou served late in the Wuding era as steward of the heir apparent's household and later joined Wei Shou in compiling the history.

sentences.zh: 景遠字叔遐，重然諾，好施與。

translations.literal: Jingyuan, styled Shuxia, highly valued his promises and loved to give generously.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jingyuan, styled Shuxia, held his word sacred and loved to give generously.

sentences.zh: 頻歲凶儉，分贍宗親；

translations.literal: In years of repeated famine and shortage, he divided provisions to support his clansmen;
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine he shared his stores with his kin;

sentences.zh: 又於通衢以飼餓者，存濟甚眾。

translations.literal: moreover along the highway he fed the hungry, saving and succoring very many.
translations.idiomatic: and along the main roads he fed the hungry, saving countless lives.

sentences.zh: 平原劉郁行經齊、兗之境，忽遇劫賊，已殺十餘人。

translations.literal: Liu Yu of Pingyuan, traveling through the territory of Qi and Yan, suddenly encountered robbers who had already killed more than ten people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu of Pingyuan, traveling through Qi and Yan, suddenly fell in with bandits who had already killed more than ten people.

sentences.zh: 次至郁，呼曰：「與君鄉近，何忍見殺。

translations.literal: When their turn came to Yu, he called out: "We are near neighbors; how can you bear to see me killed?
translations.idiomatic: When they came to Yu, he cried out, "We are from neighboring districts; how can you bear to kill me?

sentences.zh: 」賊曰：「若言鄉里，親親是誰？

translations.literal: " The bandits said: "If you speak of neighboring districts, who among your kinfolk is who?
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits said, "If you claim kin from nearby, name your relatives.

sentences.zh: 」鬱曰：「齊州主簿房陽是我姨兄。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Fang Yang, chief clerk of Qizhou, is my elder cousin on my mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu said, "Fang Yang, chief clerk of Qizhou, is my elder cousin on my mother's side.

sentences.zh: 」陽是景遠小字。

translations.literal: " Yang was Jingyuan's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang was Jingyuan's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「我食其粥得活，何得殺其親。

translations.literal: The bandits said: "I ate his gruel and lived; how could I kill his kin?
translations.idiomatic: One bandit said, "I lived on his gruel; how could I kill his kin?

sentences.zh: 」遂還衣物，蒙活者二十餘人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they returned clothing, and more than twenty people were spared and lived.
translations.idiomatic: " They returned the travelers' goods, and more than twenty lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 景遠好史傳，不為章句。

translations.literal: Jingyuan loved historical biographies and did not practice exegetical commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jingyuan loved history and biography and cared little for textual glossing.

sentences.zh: 天性小急，不類家風。

translations.literal: By nature he was slightly quick-tempered and did not resemble the family style.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was a little quick-tempered and did not resemble the family's usual manner.

sentences.zh: 然事二兄至謹，撫養兄孤，恩訓甚篤。

translations.literal: Yet in serving his two elder brothers he was utmost in care; he raised his elder brothers' orphans with affectionate instruction very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he served his two elder brothers with the utmost care and raised their orphaned children with devoted affection and instruction.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史傅豎眼慕其名義，啟為昭武府功曹參軍。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Fu Shuyan admired his reputation and integrity and memorialized that he be made Army Aide of the Zhaowu Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan, inspector of Yizhou, admired his reputation and recommended him as army aide on the Zhaowu staff.

sentences.zh: 以母老不應，豎眼頗恨之。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he did not accept; Shuyan was rather resentful of this.
translations.idiomatic: He declined because his mother was elderly, and Shuyan resented the refusal.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子敬道，永熙中開府參軍。

translations.literal: His son Jingdao, in the Yongxi era, was Staff Officer of the Opening of a Government.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang Jingdao served in the Yongxi era as staff officer on an opening-of-government staff.

sentences.zh: 畢眾敬，小名奈，東平須昌人也。

translations.literal: Bi Zhongjing, childhood name Nai, was a native of Xuchang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhongjing, childhood name Nai, came from Xuchang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 少好弓馬射獵，交結輕果，常於疆境盜掠為業。

translations.literal: In youth he loved bows, horses, hunting, and shooting; he associated with reckless daredevils and regularly made border raiding and plunder his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved horsemanship, archery, and the hunt, ran with reckless men, and made a living raiding across the border.

sentences.zh: 仕宋，位太山太守。

translations.literal: He served the Song and held the post of Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Liu Song as administrator of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 湘東王彧殺其主子業而自立，是為明帝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong, Yu, killed his lord Ziye and established himself; this was Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong, Liu Yu, killed his nephew Emperor Ziye and seized the throne as Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 遣眾敬詣兗州募人。

translations.literal: He dispatched Zhongjing to go to Yanzhou to recruit men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Zhongjing to Yanzhou to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 到彭城，刺史薛安都召與密謀，云：「晉安有上流之名，且孝武第三子，當共卿西從晉安。

translations.literal: Arriving at Pengcheng, Inspector Xue Andou summoned him for secret counsel and said: "The Prince of Jin'an has the name of legitimacy above the stream, and moreover is the third son of Emperor Xiaowu; we should together with you, sir, follow Jin'an westward.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Pengcheng, Inspector Xue Andou summoned him to a secret council and said, "The Prince of Jin'an has rightful claim to the throne and is moreover the third son of Emperor Xiaowu. Let us go west together to join him.

sentences.zh: 」眾敬從之。

translations.literal: " Zhongjing followed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongjing agreed.

sentences.zh: 東平太守申纂據無鹽城，不與之同。

translations.literal: Administrator of Dongping Shen Zuan held Wuyan city and did not join them.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zuan, administrator of Dongping, held Wuyan city and refused to join them.

sentences.zh: 及宋明平子勳，授纂兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Song pacified Zixun, he appointed Zuan Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming defeated Zixun, he made Shen Zuan inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會有人發眾敬父墓，令其母骸首散落。

translations.literal: By chance someone opened Zhongjing's father's tomb, causing his mother's bones and skull to scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then desecrated Zhongjing's father's tomb and scattered his mother's bones.

sentences.zh: 眾敬發喪行服，疑纂所為。

translations.literal: Zhongjing opened the mourning and wore mourning garments, suspecting it was Zuan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing went into mourning for the desecration and suspected Shen Zuan.

sentences.zh: 弟眾愛，為薛安都長史，亦遣人密至濟陰，掘纂父墓，以相報答。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhongai, who was Chief Clerk to Xue Andou, also sent men secretly to Jiyin to dig up Zuan's father's tomb in mutual retaliation.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhongai, chief clerk to Xue Andou, secretly sent men to Jiyin to desecrate Shen Zuan's father's tomb in retaliation.

sentences.zh: 及安都以城入魏，眾敬不同其謀。

translations.literal: When Andou surrendered the city to Wei, Zhongjing did not agree with the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Andou surrendered Pengcheng to Northern Wei, Zhongjing would not join the plot.

sentences.zh: 子元賓以母並百口悉在彭城，恐交致禍，日夜啼泣，遣請眾敬，眾敬猶未從之。

translations.literal: His son Yuanbin, because his mother and all hundred mouths of the family were in Pengcheng, feared mutual involvement would bring disaster; day and night he wept and sent to beg Zhongjing, but Zhongjing still did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanbin, knowing that his mother and the entire family of more than a hundred souls were in Pengcheng, feared disaster and wept day and night, begging Zhongjing to yield, but Zhongjing still refused.

sentences.zh: 眾敬先已遣表謝宋，宋明授眾敬兗州刺史，而以元賓有他罪，獨不舍之。

translations.literal: Zhongjing had already sent a memorial submitting to the Song; Emperor Ming of Song appointed Zhongjing Inspector of Yanzhou, but because Yuanbin had another offense, alone did not pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing had already sent a memorial submitting to the Song court; Emperor Ming made him inspector of Yanzhou but, because Yuanbin stood accused of another crime, alone refused to pardon him.

sentences.zh: 眾敬拔刀破柱曰：「皓首之年，唯有此子，今不原貸，何用獨全！

translations.literal: Zhongjing drew his sword and split a pillar, saying: "In my white-haired years I have only this son; if you do not pardon him now, what use is it for me alone to be spared whole!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing drew his sword and struck a pillar, crying, "In my old age I have only this one son. If you will not pardon him, what use is there in sparing me alone!

sentences.zh: 」及尉元至，乃以城降。

translations.literal: " When Wenyuan of the Wei arrived, then he surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wei general Wenyuan arrived, he at last surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 元遣將入城，事定。

translations.literal: Wenyuan dispatched a general to enter the city, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan sent a general into the city and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 眾敬悔恚，數日不食。

translations.literal: Zhongjing repented and was enraged; for several days he did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing was consumed with remorse and rage and went days without eating.

sentences.zh: 皇興初，就拜散騎常侍、兗州刺史，賜爵東平公，與中書侍郎李璨對為刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangxing he was directly appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Dispersed Cavalry and Inspector of Yanzhou, granted the title Duke of Dongping, and paired with Secretariat Drafter Li Can as co-inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huangxing reign he was made attendant-in-ordinary of the dispersed cavalry and inspector of Yanzhou, created Duke of Dongping, and paired with Secretariat drafter Li Can as co-inspectors.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜攻克無鹽，獲申纂，無殺纂意。

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao captured Wuyan and took Shen Zuan prisoner; he had no intention of killing Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao took Wuyan and captured Shen Zuan, with no intention of killing him.

sentences.zh: 而城中火起，纂為所燒死。

translations.literal: But fire broke out in the city, and Zuan was burned to death in it.
translations.idiomatic: But fire broke out in the city, and Shen Zuan burned to death in the blaze.

sentences.zh: 眾敬聞克無鹽，懼不殺纂，乃與白曜書，並表朝廷，雲家酷由纂。

translations.literal: Zhongjing heard that Wuyan had been taken and feared Zuan would not be killed; he then wrote to Baiyao and also memorialized the court, saying the cruelty to his family was due to Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongjing heard Wuyan had fallen, he feared Shen Zuan would be spared; he wrote to Baiyao and memorialized the court, declaring that Zuan was responsible for the cruelty done to his family.

sentences.zh: 聞纂死。

translations.literal: When he heard Zuan was dead.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Shen Zuan was dead,

sentences.zh: 乃悅。

translations.literal: Then he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: he was pleased.

sentences.zh: 二年，與薛安都朝京師，賜甲第一區。

translations.literal: In the second year, together with Xue Andou he attended court at the capital and was granted one first-grade suit of armor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he went with Xue Andou to attend court at the capital and was granted a first-class suit of armor.

sentences.zh: 後復為兗州刺史，征還京師。

translations.literal: Later he was again made Inspector of Yanzhou and summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again appointed inspector of Yanzhou and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 眾敬善自奉養，食膳豐華，必致他方遠味。

translations.literal: Zhongjing was skilled at maintaining himself; his meals were sumptuous and fine, and he always procured exotic flavors from distant places.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing took excellent care of himself. His table was lavish, and he always procured rare delicacies from distant regions.

sentences.zh: 年已七十，發須皓白，而氣力未衰，跨鞍馳騁，有若少壯。

translations.literal: Though already seventy, his hair and beard were snow-white, yet his strength had not declined; mounted on horseback he galloped as if still in his prime.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was already seventy, with hair and beard snow-white, his strength had not faded; in the saddle he could still gallop like a young man.

sentences.zh: 篤於姻類，深有國士之風。

translations.literal: Deeply devoted to his kin and in-laws, he bore the true bearing of a man of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply devoted to his kin and in-laws, he had the bearing of a true man of honor.

sentences.zh: 張讜之亡，躬往營視，有若至親。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yan died, he went in person to arrange the funeral and attend to matters as if dealing with his closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yan died, he went in person to oversee the funeral arrangements as though for his own closest kin.

sentences.zh: 太和中，孝文賓禮舊老，眾敬與高允引至方山。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, Emperor Xiaowen honored the elderly veterans as guests; Zhongjing and Gao Yun were brought to Mount Fang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe reign, Emperor Xiaowen treated the aged veterans as honored guests and had Zhongjing and Gao Yun brought to Mount Fang.

sentences.zh: 雖文武奢儉，好尚不同，然亦與允甚相愛敬，接膝談款，有若平生。

translations.literal: Though one was martial and one literary, one lavish and one frugal, and their tastes differed, yet they deeply loved and respected each other, sitting knee to knee in intimate talk as in days gone by.
translations.idiomatic: Though one was martial and one literary, one lavish and one austere, and their tastes differed, they cherished and respected each other deeply, talking knee to knee with the easy intimacy of old friends.

sentences.zh: 後以篤老，乞還桑梓，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: Later, because of his great age, he begged to return to his home district, and the court granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on account of his advanced age, he asked to return home, and the court consented.

sentences.zh: 眾敬臨還，獻真珠榼四具、銀裝劍一口、刺彪矛一枚、仙人文綾一百疋。

translations.literal: As Zhongjing was about to return, he presented four pearl-inlaid vessels, one silver-mounted sword, one tiger-embroidered spear, and one hundred bolts of celestial-pattern silk.
translations.idiomatic: Before his departure Zhongjing presented four pearl-inlaid vessels, one silver-mounted sword, one spear embroidered with leaping tigers, and one hundred bolts of figured silk woven with immortals.

sentences.zh: 文明太后與帝引見於皇信堂，賜以酒饌車馬絹等，勞遣之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming and the emperor received him at the Huangxin Hall, conferred upon him wine, food, horses, carriages, silk, and the like, and comforted him on his departure.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming and the emperor received him in the Huangxin Hall, bestowed wine, food, horses, carriages, and silk, and sent him off with honors.

sentences.zh: 卒於兗州。

translations.literal: He died in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 子元賓，少豪俠有武幹，涉獵書史。

translations.literal: His son Yuanbin, in youth was bold and chivalrous with martial talent, and broadly read books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanbin was in youth bold and chivalrous, skilled in arms, and widely read in history and the classics.

sentences.zh: 與父同建勳誠，至京師，俱為上賓，賜爵須昌侯。

translations.literal: With his father he alike rendered meritorious loyalty; upon reaching the capital, both were treated as honored guests and granted the title Marquis of Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He and his father alike won distinction through loyalty; at the capital both were honored as chief guests, and he was created Marquis of Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 後拜兗州刺史，假彭城公。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Yanzhou with acting rank as Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made inspector of Yanzhou and given acting rank as Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 父子相代為本州，當世榮之。

translations.literal: Father and son served as governors of their home province in succession; their contemporaries counted it a great honor.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son governed their home province in turn, an honor their age greatly envied.

sentences.zh: 時眾敬以老還鄉，常呼元賓為使君。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongjing had returned home in old age and always addressed Yuanbin as "My Lord Governor."
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhongjing had retired home in old age and always called Yuanbin "My Lord Governor."

sentences.zh: 每元賓聽政時，乘板輿出至元賓所，先遣左右敕不聽起，觀其斷決，忻忻然喜見顏色。

translations.literal: Whenever Yuanbin held court, Zhongjing would ride out in a palanquin to Yuanbin's seat, first sending attendants to tell him not to rise, then watching his judgments with delight shining on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yuanbin held court, Zhongjing would ride out in a palanquin to his son's seat, send attendants ahead to forbid him to rise, and watch his judgments with pleased delight written on his face.

sentences.zh: 眾敬善持家業，猶能督課田產，大致儲積。

translations.literal: Zhongjing was skilled at managing the family estate and could still supervise the farming and tax collection, building up substantial stores.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing was adept at managing the family estate and could still oversee the fields and dues, amassing considerable stores.

sentences.zh: 元賓為政清平，善撫人物，百姓愛樂之。

translations.literal: Yuanbin's governance was clear and fair; he was good at comforting people, and the common folk loved and rejoiced in him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbin governed with clarity and fairness, treated people with kindness, and the common folk loved him.

sentences.zh: 以父憂解任，喪中，遙授長兼殿中尚書。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his father he resigned his post; during the mourning period he was granted at a distance the concurrent post of Director of the Palace Secretariat in the Hall of the Central Court.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on account of his father's death; during mourning he was granted the concurrent post of Director of the Palace Secretariat from afar.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈衛尉卿，諡曰平。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously made Minister of the Guard; his posthumous name was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Minister of the Guard and given the posthumous name Ping.

sentences.zh: 元賓入魏，初娶東平劉氏，有四子，祖朽、祖髦、祖歸、祖旋。

translations.literal: After Yuanbin entered Wei, he first married a Liu of Dongping and had four sons: Zuxiu, Zumao, Zugui, and Zuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanbin entered Wei he first married a Liu of Dongping, by whom he had four sons: Zuxiu, Zumao, Zugui, and Zuxuan.

sentences.zh: 賜妻元氏，生二子，祖榮、祖暉。

translations.literal: His granted consort, née Yuan, bore two sons: Zurong and Zuhui.
translations.idiomatic: His imperially granted wife, née Yuan, bore two sons: Zurong and Zuhui.

sentences.zh: 祖朽最長，祖暉次祖髦。

translations.literal: Zuxiu was the eldest; Zuhui ranked next after Zumao.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxiu was the eldest; Zuhui ranked after Zumao in age.

sentences.zh: 故事，前妻雖先有子，後賜之妻子皆承嫡。

translations.literal: By precedent, even if the former wife had had sons first, the sons of the later granted wife all succeeded as the legitimate heirs.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, even when an earlier wife had borne sons first, the sons of the later imperially granted wife were all treated as legitimate heirs.

sentences.zh: 所以劉氏先亡，祖暉不服重。

translations.literal: For this reason, because the Liu clan wife had died first, Zuhui did not observe full mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, because Lady Liu had died first, Zuhui did not observe full mourning for her.

sentences.zh: 元氏後卒，祖朽等三年終禮。

translations.literal: When the Yuan clan wife died later, Zuxiu and the others completed the three-year mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Yuan died later, Zuxiu and the others completed the full three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 祖榮早卒，子義允襲祖爵東平公，例降為侯。

translations.literal: Zurong died early; his son Yiyun inherited the grandfather's title Duke of Dongping, which by regulation was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Zurong died young; his son Yiyun inherited the grandfather's title of Duke of Dongping, reduced by regulation to marquis.

sentences.zh: 卒，子僧安襲。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Seng'an inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his son Seng'an succeeded.

sentences.zh: 祖朽身長八尺，腰帶十圍。

translations.literal: Zuxiu was eight chi tall with a waist ten wei in girth.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxiu stood eight chi tall, with a girth of ten wei about the waist.

sentences.zh: 涉獵經史，好為文詠，善與人交。

translations.literal: He broadly read the classics and histories, loved composing literary verse, and was skilled at friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged widely in the classics and histories, loved literary composition, and made friends easily.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵須昌侯，例降為伯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's title Marquis of Xuchang, which by regulation was reduced to earl.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's marquisate of Xuchang, reduced by regulation to earl.

sentences.zh: 以本州中正為統軍，隸邢巒討梁師，以功封南城縣男。

translations.literal: As rectifier of his home province he served as commander-in-chief under Xing Luan in campaigns against Liang forces, and for merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Nancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: As provincial rectifier he served as commander-in-chief under Xing Luan against Liang armies and was enfeoffed Baron of Nancheng County for his merits.

sentences.zh: 曆散騎侍郎、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry and Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry and Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 神龜末，除東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shengui era he was appointed Inspector of Eastern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Shengui reign he was made inspector of Eastern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖朽善撫邊，清平有信，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: Zuxiu was skilled at pacifying the frontier, was clear, fair, and trustworthy, and the people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxiu governed the frontier with skill, fairness, and integrity, and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 後為瀛州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was made Inspector of Yingzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made inspector of Yingzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 無子，以弟祖歸子義暢為後，襲爵。

translations.literal: Having no son, he took his younger brother Zugui's son Yichang as heir, who inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son and adopted his younger brother Zugui's son Yichang as heir, who inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 義暢傾巧無士業，善通時要，位中書侍郎、兗州大中正。

translations.literal: Yichang was artful and scheming with no scholarly occupation; skilled at mastering the needs of the times, he rose to Secretariat Drafter and Grand Rectifier of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yichang was cunning and unscrupulous, without scholarly calling, but skilled at reading the times; he rose to Secretariat Drafter and grand rectifier of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 後除散騎常待，坐事伏法。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Dispersed Cavalry but was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made attendant-in-ordinary of the dispersed cavalry but was executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 祖髦以兄祖朽別封南城，以須昌伯回授之，位東平太守，卒于本州別駕。

translations.literal: Zumao, because his elder brother Zuxiu was separately enfeoffed at Nancheng, was granted the Xuchang earldom in return, rose to Administrator of Dongping, and died while serving as Vice Inspector of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother Zuxiu had been separately enfeoffed at Nancheng, Zumao was given the Xuchang earldom in exchange; he rose to administrator of Dongping and died while serving as vice inspector of his home province.

sentences.zh: 祖暉早有器幹，為豳州刺史，以全守勳，封新昌縣子。

translations.literal: Zuhui early showed talent and capability; as Inspector of Binzhou he was enfeoffed Viscount of Xinchang County for merit in holding the city intact.
translations.idiomatic: Zuhui showed talent and capability early; as inspector of Binzhou he was enfeoffed Viscount of Xinchang County for successfully holding his post.

sentences.zh: 逢蕭寶夤退敗，祖暉拔城，東趣華陰，坐免官爵。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin suffered defeat and retreated, Zuhui abandoned the city and fled east toward Huayin; for this he was dismissed and stripped of title.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin was routed in retreat, Zuhui abandoned the city and fled east toward Huayin; he was dismissed and stripped of rank for it.

sentences.zh: 尋行豳州事。

translations.literal: Soon he was entrusted with the affairs of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was put in charge of Binzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 建義中，詔復州、爵。

translations.literal: During the Jianyi era, an edict restored his provincial post and title.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyi era an edict restored his provincial post and title.

sentences.zh: 後為賊宿勤明達所攻沒。

translations.literal: Later he was attacked and overrun by the bandit Suqin Mingda.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was overrun in an attack by the rebel Suqin Mingda.

sentences.zh: 長子義勰襲爵，齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yixie inherited the title; when Qi received the abdication, the title was reduced by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yixie inherited the title; when Qi took the throne the title was reduced by regulation.

sentences.zh: 義勰弟義云。

translations.literal: Yixie's younger brother was Yiyun.
translations.idiomatic: Yixie's younger brother was Yiyun.

sentences.zh: 義雲小字陀兒，少粗俠。

translations.literal: Yiyun's childhood name was Tuo'er; in youth he was rough and chivalrous.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyun, styled Tuo'er, was rough and chivalrous in youth.

sentences.zh: 家在兗州北境，常劫掠行旅，州裏患之。

translations.literal: His family lived on the northern border of Yanzhou and often robbed travelers; the prefecture was troubled by them.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived on Yanzhou's northern frontier and often robbed travelers; the prefecture found them a plague.

sentences.zh: 晚方折節從官，累遷尚書都官郎中。

translations.literal: Only late in life did he reform his ways and enter official service, rising in succession to Director of the Capital Crimes Bureau in the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: Only late did he reform his ways and enter office, rising in turn to director of the Capital Crimes Bureau in the Ministry of State.

sentences.zh: 性嚴酷，事多幹了。

translations.literal: His nature was harsh and cruel; in affairs he was largely capable and effective.
translations.idiomatic: He was harsh by nature and generally efficient in affairs.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄作相，以為稱職，令普勾偽官，專以車輻考掠，所獲甚多，然大起怨謗。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang of Qi became chancellor, he found Yiyun suited to the task and ordered a general round-up of false officials; Yiyun relied exclusively on torture with cart-wheel spokes, catching many, but aroused widespread resentment and slander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang of Qi became chancellor he found Yiyun well suited to the task and ordered a general hunt for false officials; Yiyun tortured suspects with cart-wheel spokes, uncovering many cases but stirring widespread hatred.

sentences.zh: 曾為司州吏所訟，雲其有所減截，並改換文書。

translations.literal: Once he was sued by an official of Sizhou, who accused him of embezzling funds and altering documents.
translations.idiomatic: Once an official of Sizhou sued him, claiming he had skimmed funds and falsified documents.

sentences.zh: 文襄以其推偽，眾人怨望，並無所問。

translations.literal: Wenxiang, because he had exposed false officials, and because the people resented him, asked nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang, since Yiyun's work had exposed false officials and the public was already hostile to him, investigated nothing.

sentences.zh: 乃拘吏，數而斬之。

translations.literal: Instead he seized the official, listed his crimes, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he seized the accuser, condemned him, and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 因此銳情訊鞫，威名日盛。

translations.literal: Because of this he grew sharper in interrogation and torture, and his fearsome reputation daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he threw himself into interrogation with redoubled zeal, and his fearsome reputation grew daily.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，除書侍御史，彈射不避勳親。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan accepted the abdication, Yiyun was appointed Palace Attendant Censor and impeached without sparing meritorious kin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan took the throne Yiyun was made palace attendant censor and impeached without sparing even meritorious kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 累選御史中丞，繩劾更切。

translations.literal: Repeatedly selected as Chief Censor, his prosecutions grew even sharper.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to chief censor, and his prosecutions grew even harsher.

sentences.zh: 然豪橫不平，頻被怨訟。

translations.literal: Yet he was domineering and unjust and was frequently sued in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was domineering and unjust and was frequently sued in bitterness.

sentences.zh: 前為汲郡太守翟嵩啟列：義雲從父兄僧明負官債，先任京畿長史，不受其屬，立限切征，由此挾嫌，數遣御史過郡訪察，欲相推繩。

translations.literal: Previously when serving as Administrator of Ji Commandery, Zhai Song memorialized listing that Yiyun's elder cousin on his father's side Sengming owed official debts; Sengming had previously served as Chief Secretary of the Capital Region and had refused to accept his subordinates; Yiyun set a strict deadline for collection and, bearing a grudge on this account, repeatedly sent censors through the commandery to investigate, seeking to prosecute him.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, as administrator of Ji Commandery, Zhai Song had memorialized the throne that Yiyun's elder male cousin Sengming owed official debts; Sengming had once served as chief secretary of the capital region and had refused Yiyun's authority; Yiyun set a harsh deadline for collection and, nursing a grudge, repeatedly sent censors through the commandery to investigate, seeking to prosecute him.

sentences.zh: 又坐私藏工匠，家有十餘機織錦，並造金銀器物，乃被禁止。

translations.literal: He was also charged with privately harboring artisans; his household had more than ten looms weaving brocade and also made gold and silver wares, and he was placed under detention.
translations.idiomatic: He was also charged with keeping craftsmen in private employ: more than ten looms in his house wove brocade, and he also produced gold and silver goods; he was placed under detention.

sentences.zh: 尋見釋，以為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was released and appointed Left Chief Secretary to the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was released and made left chief secretary to the Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 子瑞從兄消難為北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Zirui's elder cousin Xiaonan was Inspector of Northern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zirui's elder male cousin Xiaonan was inspector of Northern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 義雲遣御史張子階詣州采風聞，先禁其典簽家客等。

translations.literal: Yiyun sent Censor Zhang Zijie to the province to gather rumors, first imprisoning Xiaonan's registry clerks, household retainers, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyun sent censor Zhang Zijie to the province to gather intelligence, first detaining Xiaonan's registry clerks and household retainers.

sentences.zh: 消難危懼，遂叛入周。

translations.literal: Xiaonan, stricken with fear, then defected to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xiaonan defected to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 時論歸罪義雲，雲其規報子瑞。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion blamed Yiyun, saying he had plotted revenge against Zirui.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion blamed Yiyun, claiming he had plotted revenge against Zirui.

sentences.zh: 事亦上聞。

translations.literal: The matter also reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The matter also reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 爾前宴賞，義雲常預，從此後集見稍疏，聲望大損。

translations.literal: Before this, at banquets and rewards Yiyun was always present; from then on he was seen at gatherings somewhat less often, and his renown greatly suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Before this Yiyun had always been present at imperial feasts and rewards; thereafter he was seen at court somewhat less often, and his prestige suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，子瑞遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ganming era, Zirui was transferred to Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Ganming era Zirui was made chief censor.

sentences.zh: 鄭子默正被任用，義雲之姑即子默祖母，遂除度支尚書，攝左丞。

translations.literal: Zheng Zimo was then in favor; Yiyun's paternal aunt was Zimo's grandmother, and so Yiyun was appointed Minister of Revenue and acted as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zimo was then in high favor; Yiyun's paternal aunt was Zimo's grandmother, and Yiyun was accordingly made Minister of Revenue and acting left vice director.

sentences.zh: 子默誅後，左丞便解。

translations.literal: After Zimo was executed, the acting left vice directorship was dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: After Zimo was executed the acting left vice directorship ended.

sentences.zh: 孝昭赴晉陽，高元海留鄴，義雲深相依附。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao went to Jinyang, Gao Yuanhai remained at Ye; Yiyun attached himself deeply to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao went to Jinyang, Gao Yuanhai remained at Ye, and Yiyun clung closely to him.

sentences.zh: 知其信向釋氏，常隨之聽講，為此款密，無所不至。

translations.literal: Knowing that Yuanhai was a devout follower of Buddhism, he often followed him to hear lectures; in such intimate friendship nothing was held back.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yuanhai's devotion to Buddhism, he often accompanied him to hear lectures; in this close bond nothing was held back.

sentences.zh: 及孝昭大漸，顧命武成。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao was near death, he entrusted the succession to Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao lay dying he entrusted the throne to Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 高歸彥至都，武成猶致疑惑。

translations.literal: When Gao Guiyan arrived at the capital, Wucheng still harbored doubts.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Guiyan reached the capital Wucheng still held doubts.

sentences.zh: 元海遣犢車迎義雲入北宮參審，遂與元海等勸進。

translations.literal: Yuanhai sent an ox-cart to bring Yiyun into the Northern Palace to join in deliberation, and together with Yuanhai and others urged Wucheng to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai sent an ox-cart to bring Yiyun into the Northern Palace to deliberate, and together with Yuanhai and others urged Wucheng to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 仍從幸晉陽，參預時政。

translations.literal: He then accompanied the emperor to Jinyang and took part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then accompanied the emperor to Jinyang and took part in governance.

sentences.zh: 尋除兗州刺史，給後部鼓吹，即本州也。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Inspector of Yanzhou and granted rear guard musicians -- his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made inspector of Yanzhou and granted rear guard musicians -- his native province.

sentences.zh: 軒昂自得，意望銓衡之舉，見諸人自陳，逆許引接。

translations.literal: High-spirited and self-satisfied, he looked forward to appointments in personnel selection; when people came to present themselves, he would bluntly promise them posts and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and self-satisfied, he looked to wield power over appointments; when men came to recommend themselves he bluntly promised them posts and took them in.

sentences.zh: 又言離別暫時，非久在州。

translations.literal: He also said his leave-taking was temporary and that he would not long remain in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He also said his departure would be brief and that he would not remain long in the province.

sentences.zh: 先有鐃吹，至於按部行遊，兩部並用。

translations.literal: He already had cymbals and pipes; when touring his jurisdiction on inspection, he used both bands together.
translations.idiomatic: He already had cymbals and pipes; on inspection tours he employed both bands at once.

sentences.zh: 猶作書與元海，論敘時事。

translations.literal: He still wrote letters to Yuanhai discussing current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He still wrote to Yuanhai discussing affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 元海入內，不覺遺落，給事中李孝貞得而奏之。

translations.literal: When Yuanhai entered the palace he unknowingly dropped one; Supervising Secretary Li Xiaozhen found it and memorialized it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhai entered the palace he dropped one without noticing; supervising secretary Li Xiaozhen found it and memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 為此，元海漸疏，孝貞因是兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Because of this Yuanhai gradually fell from favor, and Xiaozhen thereby also gained the concurrent post of Drafter of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Yuanhai gradually lost favor, and Xiaozhen thereby gained the concurrent post of secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 又高歸彥起逆，義雲在州私集人馬，並聚甲仗，將以自防，實無他意，為人密啟。

translations.literal: Again, when Gao Guiyan rose in rebellion, Yiyun privately gathered men and horses in the province and also amassed arms and armor, intending only self-defense and truly with no other design, but someone secretly reported him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Guiyan rebelled, Yiyun privately gathered men and horses in the province and stockpiled arms, intending only self-defense and with no other purpose, but someone secretly denounced him.

sentences.zh: 及歸彥被擒，又列其朋黨專擅，為此追還。

translations.literal: When Guiyan was captured, others also listed his faction's monopolization of power, and for this Yiyun was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Guiyan was captured, others also denounced his faction's monopoly of power, and Yiyun was recalled for it.

sentences.zh: 武成猶錄其往誠，竟不加罪，除兼七兵尚書。

translations.literal: Wucheng still credited his past loyalty and in the end did not punish him, appointing him concurrent Minister of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng still credited his past loyalty and did not punish him in the end, appointing him concurrent Minister of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 義雲性豪縱，頗以施惠為心。

translations.literal: Yiyun's nature was lavish and unrestrained; he tended rather to take delight in showing generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyun was by nature extravagant and unrestrained, and rather prided himself on generosity.

sentences.zh: 累世本州刺史，家富於財，士之匱乏者，多有拯濟。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been governors of their home province and was rich in wealth; many scholars in want he rescued and supported.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had governed Yanzhou and was wealthy; he aided and supported many needy scholars.

sentences.zh: 及貴，恣情驕侈，營造第宅宏壯，未幾而成。

translations.literal: Once he rose high, he indulged himself in pride and extravagance, constructing a mansion vast and grand that was finished in no time.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated he gave free rein to pride and luxury, building a vast mansion that was finished in no time.

sentences.zh: 閨門穢雜，聲遍朝野。

translations.literal: His household was disorderly and licentious; the reputation spread through court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: His household was disorderly and dissolute, and the scandal spread through court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 為郎時，與左丞宋遊道因公事忿競。

translations.literal: When he was a director, he clashed in anger with Left Vice Director Song Youdao over official business.
translations.idiomatic: When he was a director he quarreled angrily with left vice director Song Youdao over official business.

sentences.zh: 遊道廷辱之，云：「《雄狐》之詩，千載為汝。

translations.literal: Youdao humiliated him in court, saying: "The ode of the male fox -- a thousand years it has waited for you.
translations.idiomatic: In court Youdao humiliated him, saying, "The ode of the male fox -- a thousand years it has waited for you.

sentences.zh: 」義雲一無所答。

translations.literal: " Yiyun answered not a word.
translations.idiomatic: " Yiyun made no reply whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 然酷暴殘忍，非人理所及。

translations.literal: Yet he was cruel, violent, and ruthless beyond what human reason could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was cruel, violent, and ruthless beyond ordinary human measure.

sentences.zh: 為家尤甚，子姓僕隸，恆瘡痍遍體。

translations.literal: At home it was worst of all; sons, clan members, and servants and slaves constantly bore wounds all over their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: At home it was worst of all: sons, clansmen, and servants were constantly covered in wounds.

sentences.zh: 有孽子善昭，性至凶頑，與義雲侍婢奸通。

translations.literal: He had a bastard son Shanzhao, whose nature was extremely vicious and stubborn; he had an illicit affair with Yiyun's maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: He had a bastard son, Shanzhao, who was vicious and incorrigible by nature and carried on an affair with one of Yiyun's maidservants.

sentences.zh: 搒掠無數，為其著籠頭，系之庭樹，食以芻秣，十餘日乃釋之。

translations.literal: He flogged and tortured him countless times, put a head-cage on him, tied him to a courtyard tree, fed him fodder, and only released him after more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: He beat and tortured him without count, put a head-cage on him, tied him to a tree in the courtyard, fed him fodder, and did not release him until more than ten days had passed.

sentences.zh: 夜中，義雲被賊害，即善昭所佩刀也，遺之於善昭庭中。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night Yiyun was slain by bandits; the weapon was Shanzhao's own sword, which was left in Shanzhao's courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In the night Yiyun was murdered by bandits with Shanzhao's own sword, which was left in Shanzhao's courtyard.

sentences.zh: 善昭聞難奔哭。

translations.literal: Shanzhao, hearing of the calamity, ran to weep.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the murder, Shanzhao ran to the scene weeping.

sentences.zh: 家人得佩刀，善昭怖，便走出，投平恩墅舍。

translations.literal: When the household found the sword, Shanzhao was terrified and fled at once, taking refuge at the Ping'en villa estate.
translations.idiomatic: When the household recovered the sword, Shanzhao was terrified and fled at once to the Ping'en villa estate.

sentences.zh: 旦日，武成令舍人是蘭子暢就宅推之。

translations.literal: The next morning Wucheng sent his palace attendant Lan Zichang to his residence to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning Wucheng sent his palace attendant Lan Zichang to investigate at the residence.

sentences.zh: 爾前，義雲新納少室范陽盧氏，有色貌。

translations.literal: Not long before, Yiyun had newly taken into his household as a concubine Lady Lu of Fanyang; she was beautiful in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly before, Yiyun had taken Lady Lu of Fanyang as a concubine; she was beautiful.

sentences.zh: 子暢疑盧奸人所為，將加栲掠。

translations.literal: Zichang suspected that Lu was the adulterer's accomplice and was about to apply torture.
translations.idiomatic: Zichang suspected Lu had been the adulterer's accomplice and was about to put her to torture.

sentences.zh: 盧具列善昭云爾。

translations.literal: Lu fully recounted Shanzhao's deeds, saying thus.
translations.idiomatic: Lu gave a full account of Shanzhao's conduct along these lines.

sentences.zh: 乃收捕，系臨漳獄，將斬之。

translations.literal: Shanzhao was then seized and imprisoned in Linzhang jail, and was to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhao was then arrested, held in Linzhang prison, and sentenced to execution.

sentences.zh: 邢邵上言，此乃大逆，義雲又是朝貴，不可發。

translations.literal: Xing Shao memorialized the throne, saying this was great treason, and since Yiyun was also a court noble, the matter must not be made public.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao memorialized that this was treason of the highest degree, and since Yiyun was a court noble the affair must not be made public.

sentences.zh: 乃斬之於獄，棄屍漳水。

translations.literal: Shanzhao was beheaded in prison and his corpse cast into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhao was beheaded in prison and his body thrown into the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 祖歸位建甯太守。

translations.literal: Zu Gui held the post of Administrator of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Gui served as administrator of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 子義遠，位平原太守。

translations.literal: His son Yiyuan held the post of Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiyuan served as administrator of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 義遠弟義顯、義攜，性並豪率。

translations.literal: Yiyuan's younger brothers Yixian and Yixie were both bold and uninhibited by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan's younger brothers Yixian and Yixie were both bold and uninhibited.

sentences.zh: 天平以後，梁使人還往，經歷兗城。

translations.literal: After the Tianping era, Liang envoys came and went, passing through Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianping era, envoys from Liang traveled back and forth through Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 前後州將以義攜兄弟善營鮭膳，器物鮮華，常兼長史，接宴賓客。

translations.literal: Governors before and after, because the Yixie brothers were skilled at preparing salmon dishes and their vessels were fresh and splendid, regularly gave them concurrent posts as chief clerk to receive and feast guests.
translations.idiomatic: Successive governors, finding the Yixie brothers adept at preparing fine salmon feasts with splendid tableware, regularly gave them concurrent posts as chief clerk to entertain guests.

sentences.zh: 祖旋，太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: Zu Xuan was Acting Aide to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xuan served as acting aide to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈都官尚書、齊兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously granted Minister of Court Affairs and Inspector of the two provinces of Qi and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Court Affairs and inspector of Qi and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 眾敬弟眾愛，隨兄歸魏，以勳為第一客，賜爵钜平侯。

translations.literal: Zhongjing's younger brother Zhong'ai followed his brother in returning to Wei; because of his merit he became the chief guest retainer and was granted the marquisate of Juping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing's younger brother Zhong'ai followed him back to Wei; for his merit he was made chief retainer and enfeoffed as Marquis of Juping.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously granted Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 諡曰康。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Kang.

sentences.zh: 子聞慰，字子安。

translations.literal: His son Wenwei, styled Zi'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenwei, styled Zi'an.

sentences.zh: 有器幹，襲爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: He had ability and capacity; he inherited the title, and by regulation it was reduced to that of a baron.
translations.idiomatic: A man of ability, he inherited the title, which by regulation was reduced to baron.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，累遷清河內史，固以疾辭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanchang he was promoted in succession to Internal Administrator of Qinghe, but firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yanchang era he rose through successive posts to internal administrator of Qinghe, but firmly declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 後試守廣平內史。

translations.literal: Later he was given a provisional appointment as Internal Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was provisionally appointed internal administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 正光初，相州刺史中山王熙起兵，謀誅元叉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguang, Yuanchang Wang Xi, Inspector of Xiangzhou, raised troops to plot the execution of Yuan Cha.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenguang era, Prince of Zhongshan Xi, inspector of Xiangzhou, raised troops in a plot to kill Yuan Cha.

sentences.zh: 聞慰斬其使，發兵拒之。

translations.literal: Wenwei beheaded his envoy and raised troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei executed his envoy and raised troops to resist him.

sentences.zh: 叉以為忠於己，遷滄州刺史，甚有政績。
