translations.literal: Cha considered him loyal to himself and transferred him to be Inspector of Cangzhou, where he achieved notable administrative results.
translations.idiomatic: Cha considered him loyal and transferred him to Cangzhou, where he achieved notable results in office.

sentences.zh: 後除散騎常侍、東道行台，尋為都督、安樂王鑒軍司馬，攻元法僧，敗。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Attendant Cavalier and Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters; soon he served as army chief of staff under the commander Prince Anle Jian, attacked Yuan Faseng, and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed attendant cavalier and eastern route mobile headquarters; soon he served as army chief of staff under Commander Prince Anle Jian, attacked Yuan Faseng, and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 奔還京師，被劾，遇赦免。

translations.literal: He fled back to the capital, was impeached, and was pardoned in an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He fled back to the capital, was impeached, and was pardoned by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈散騎常侍、兗州刺史，伯如故，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously granted Attendant Cavalier and Inspector of Yanzhou; his baronage remained as before, and his posthumous name was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made attendant cavalier and inspector of Yanzhou; his barony remained unchanged, and he was posthumously titled Gong.

sentences.zh: 子祖彥，字修賢。

translations.literal: His son Zuyan, styled Xiuxian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuyan, styled Xiuxian.

sentences.zh: 涉獵書傳，風度閒雅，為時所知。

translations.literal: He ranged widely in books and records; his bearing was relaxed and refined, and he was known in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Well read in books and records, he had a relaxed and refined bearing and was known in his day.

sentences.zh: 以侍卸史為元法僧監軍，法僧反，被逼南入。

translations.literal: As attendant censor he served as oversight commander for Yuan Faseng; when Faseng rebelled, he was compelled to flee south.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as attendant censor and oversight commander for Yuan Faseng, he was forced south when Faseng rebelled.

sentences.zh: 後還，曆中書侍郎，襲爵钜平伯。

translations.literal: Later he returned and passed through the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat, inheriting the barony of Juping.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he served as vice director of the secretariat and inherited the barony of Juping.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書右僕射、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made vice director of the right of the secretariat and inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖彥弟祖哲，秘書郎。

translations.literal: Zuyan's younger brother Zuzhe was a Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyan's younger brother Zuzhe served as secretary of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 諸畢當朝，不乏榮貴，但幃薄不修，為時所鄙。

translations.literal: The various Bi in office at court were not lacking in honor and rank, but their domestic conduct was not kept in order and they were despised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Bi clan held many posts at court and did not lack for honor, but their households were disorderly and they were despised in their time.

sentences.zh: 申纂者，本魏郡人，申鍾曾孫也。

translations.literal: Shen Zuan was originally a man of Wei Commandery, a great-grandson of Shen Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zuan was originally from Wei Commandery, a great-grandson of Shen Zhong.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，道武平中山，纂舉室南奔，家于濟陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi, Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan; Zuan moved his whole household south in flight and settled in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Huangshi era, when Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, Zuan fled south with his entire household and settled in Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 及在無鹽，仕宋為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When he was at Wuyan, he served Song as Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While at Wuyan he served the Liu Song as inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 既敗，子景義入魏。

translations.literal: After his defeat, his son Jingyi entered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat his son Jingyi entered Wei.

sentences.zh: 羊祉，字靈祐，太山钜平人，晉太僕卿琇之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Yang Zhi, styled Lingyou, was a man of Juping in Taishan, a sixth-generation descendant of Yang Xiu, Grand Master of Ceremonies of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi, styled Lingyou, was from Juping in Taishan, a sixth-generation descendant of Jin grand master of ceremonies Yang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 父規之，宋任城令。

translations.literal: His father Guizhi was Magistrate of Rencheng under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guizhi was magistrate of Rencheng under the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 太武南討，至鄒山，規之與魯郡太守崔邪利及其屬縣徐遜、愛猛之等俱降，賜爵钜平子，拜雁門太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned south and reached Zou Mountain, Guizhi together with Administrator of Lu Commandery Cui Xieli and officials of his subordinate counties Xu Xun, Ai Mengzhi, and others all surrendered; he was granted the title of Viscount of Juping and appointed Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu marched south to Zou Mountain, Guizhi surrendered together with Cui Xieli, administrator of Lu commandery, and officials of his subordinate counties including Xu Xun and Ai Mengzhi; he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Juping and appointed administrator of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 祉性剛愎，好刑名。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was stubborn and unyielding; he loved legal punishments and names.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was stubborn and unyielding by nature and fond of penal law.

sentences.zh: 為司空令、輔國長史，襲爵钜平子。

translations.literal: He served as Chief of the Ministry of Works and Chief Clerk of the Auxiliary State Army, inheriting the viscounty of Juping.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief of the ministry of works and chief clerk of the auxiliary state army, inheriting the viscounty of Juping.

sentences.zh: 侵盜公資，私營居宅，有司按之，抵死。

translations.literal: He embezzled public funds and privately built a residence; the authorities investigated and he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: He embezzled public funds to build a private residence; the authorities investigated and he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 孝文特恕遠徙。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen specially pardoned him to exile in a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen specially pardoned him to exile in a distant place.

sentences.zh: 後還。

translations.literal: Later he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned.

sentences.zh: 景明初，為將作都將，加左軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he was made Director of the Palace Construction Corps and given the additional title of General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingming era he became director of the palace construction corps and was additionally made general of the left army.

sentences.zh: 四年，持節為梁州軍司，討叛氐。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he held imperial credentials as military commander of Liangzhou to pacify rebellious Di.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was credentialed as military commander of Liangzhou to suppress rebellious Di tribes.

sentences.zh: 正始二年，王師伐蜀，以祉假節龍驤將軍、益州刺史，出劍閣而還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi the royal army attacked Shu; Zhi was given provisional imperial mandate as General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Yizhou, marched out through Jian'ge Pass and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengshi the imperial army campaigned against Shu; Zhi was appointed provisional general of agile cavalry and inspector of Yizhou, marched through Jian'ge Pass, and returned.

sentences.zh: 又以本將軍為秦、梁二州刺史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was also made Inspector of the two provinces of Qin and Liang with his original general's title, and given the additional title of General Who Captures Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made inspector of Qin and Liang with his previous general's rank and additionally titled general who captures barbarians.

sentences.zh: 天性酷忍，又不清潔，坐掠人為奴婢。

translations.literal: By nature he was cruel and ruthless, and was also not clean in conduct; he was convicted of seizing people as slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was cruel and ruthless and also corrupt; he was convicted of seizing people as slaves.

sentences.zh: 為御史中尉王顯所彈，免。

translations.literal: He was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Wang Xian impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 高肇執政，祉復被起為光祿大夫，假平南將軍、持節，領步騎三萬，先驅趣涪。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao held power, Zhi was again summoned and made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, provisional General Who Pacifies the South, with imperial credentials, leading thirty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard hastening to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao held power, Zhi was recalled as grand master for splendid happiness, made provisional general who pacifies the south with imperial credentials, and sent ahead with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry toward Fu.

sentences.zh: 未至，宣武崩，班師。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Emperor Xuanwu died and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived Emperor Xuanwu died and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夜中引軍，山有二徑，軍人迷而失路，祉便斬隊副楊明達，梟首路側。

translations.literal: At night he led the army; the mountain had two paths and the soldiers lost their way in confusion; Zhi immediately beheaded squad deputy Yang Mingda and displayed his head by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the army by night over a mountain with two paths, the soldiers lost their way; Zhi immediately beheaded squad deputy Yang Mingda and displayed his head by the road.

sentences.zh: 為中尉元昭所劾，會赦免。

translations.literal: He was impeached by Censor Yuan Zhao and was pardoned in an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yuan Zhao impeached him, but he was pardoned in an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 後加平北將軍，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: Later he was given the additional title of General Who Pacifies the North but died before accepting the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was given the additional title of general who pacifies the north but died before he could accept it.

sentences.zh: 贈安東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general who pacifies the east and inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿元端、博士劉台龍議諡曰：「祉志存埋輪，不避強禦；

translations.literal: Vice Director of Grand Sacrifices Yuan Duan and Erudite Liu Tailong proposed the posthumous name, saying: "Zhi's purpose was like burying the wheel -- he did not avoid the strong and overbearing;
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of grand sacrifices Yuan Duan and erudite Liu Tailong proposed a posthumous title, saying, "Zhi's purpose was to bury the wheel -- he did not shrink from the powerful and overbearing;

sentences.zh: 及贊戎律，熊武斯裁；

translations.literal: When he assisted in military law, he was bold as a bear in martial decisions;
translations.idiomatic: In assisting military law he was bold as a bear in martial judgment;

sentences.zh: 仗節撫籓，邊夷識德，化沾殊類，繈負懷仁。

translations.literal: Bearing credentials he pacified the frontier fief; border peoples recognized his virtue; his transforming influence reached all kinds; infants in slings felt his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing imperial credentials he pacified the frontier; border peoples recognized his virtue, his transforming influence reached all peoples, and even infants in slings felt his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 謹依諡法，布德行剛曰景，宜諡為景。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the law of posthumous names, 'spreading virtue with resolute conduct' is called Jing; he should be posthumously named Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully following the law of posthumous names, 'spreading virtue with resolute conduct' is Jing; he should be posthumously titled Jing.

sentences.zh: 」侍中侯剛、給事黃門侍郎元纂等駁曰：「臣聞唯名與器，弗可妄假。

translations.literal: " Attendant-in-Ordinary Hou Gang, Supervising Master of Affairs and Yellow Gate Vice Director Yuan Zuan, and others objected, saying: "We have heard that names and insignia may not be recklessly bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendant-in-ordinary Hou Gang, supervising master of affairs and yellow gate vice director Yuan Zuan, and others objected, saying, "We have heard that names and insignia may not be recklessly bestowed.

sentences.zh: 定諡准行，必當其跡。

translations.literal: When fixing a posthumous name by conduct, it must match his deeds.
translations.idiomatic: When assigning a posthumous name according to conduct, it must match his actual deeds.

sentences.zh: 按祉志性急酷，所在過威，布德罕聞，暴聲屢發。

translations.literal: Investigating Zhi, his disposition was harsh and cruel; wherever he served he exceeded in severity; spreading virtue was rarely heard of; reports of violence arose repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: On investigation Zhi's disposition was harsh and cruel; wherever he served he exceeded in severity; spreading virtue was rarely heard of, and reports of violence arose again and again.

sentences.zh: 而禮官虛述，諡之為景，非直失於一人，實毀朝則。

translations.literal: Yet the ritual officials gave empty praise and would posthumously name him Jing; this is not merely an error regarding one man -- it truly destroys the standards of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ritual officials wrote empty praise and would posthumously title him Jing; this is not merely an error about one man but truly undermines court standards.

sentences.zh: 請還付外，准行更量虛實。

translations.literal: We ask that the matter be returned to the outer offices to measure truth and falsehood again according to conduct.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the matter be returned to the outer offices to reweigh truth and falsehood according to conduct.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后令曰：「依駁便議。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "In accordance with the objection, reconsider and decide.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Dowager Ling ordered, "In accordance with the objection, reconsider and decide.

sentences.zh: 」元端、台龍上言：「竊惟諡者行之跡，狀者跡之稱。

translations.literal: " Yuan Duan and Tailong memorialized: "We humbly consider that the posthumous name is the trace of conduct, and the epitaph is the name of that trace.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Duan and Tailong memorialized, "We humbly consider that the posthumous name is the trace of conduct, and the epitaph is the name of that trace.

sentences.zh: 然尚書銓衡是司，厘品庶物，若狀與跡乖，應抑而不受，錄其實狀，然後下寺，依諡法准狀科上。

translations.literal: Yet the Ministry of Personnel is in charge of weighing and measuring; it grades all things. If the epitaph and the trace disagree, it should be suppressed and not accepted; the true facts should be recorded, and only then sent down to the temples to assign a name according to the law of posthumous names based on the epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Ministry of Personnel weighs and grades all things; if the epitaph and the record of conduct disagree, it should be rejected, the true facts recorded, and only then sent to the temples to assign a name according to the law of posthumous names based on the epitaph.

sentences.zh: 豈有舍其行跡，外有所求，去狀去稱，將何所准。

translations.literal: How could one abandon his conduct and traces, seek something from outside, discard epitaph and designation -- on what basis would one decide?
translations.idiomatic: How could one set aside his conduct and records, seek something from outside, discard epitaph and designation -- on what basis would one decide?

sentences.zh: 檢祉以母老辭籓，乃降手詔云：'卿綏撫有年，聲實兼著，安邊寧境，實稱朝望。

translations.literal: Examining the records: when Zhi declined his frontier post because his mother was old, an imperial hand-edict was issued, saying: 'You have pacified and comforted the people for years; your reputation and achievement are both notable; securing the border and settling the frontier truly match the court's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the records: when Zhi declined his frontier post because his mother was old, an imperial hand-edict was issued, saying, 'You have pacified and comforted the people for years; your reputation and achievement are both notable; securing the border and settling the frontier truly match the court's hopes.

sentences.zh: '及其沒也，又加顯贈，言祉誠著累朝，效彰出內，作牧岷區，字萌之績驟聞。

translations.literal: ' At his death an eminent posthumous grant was also added, stating that Zhi's loyalty was evident across several reigns, his achievements known within and without, governing the Min region where the fruits of his policies spread quickly.
translations.idiomatic: ' At his death an eminent posthumous grant was also added, stating that Zhi's loyalty was evident across several reigns, his achievements known within and without, governing the Min region where the fruits of his policies spread quickly.

sentences.zh: 詔冊褒美，無替倫望。

translations.literal: Imperial edicts and grants praised him without diminishing his standing among peers.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts and grants praised him without diminishing his standing among peers.

sentences.zh: 然君子使人，器之，義無求備。

translations.literal: Yet the gentleman employs men according to their capacities; righteousness does not demand completeness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the gentleman employs men according to their capacities; one ought not demand perfection.

sentences.zh: 德有數德，優劣不同，剛而能克，亦為德焉。

translations.literal: Virtue has many kinds; superior and inferior differ; to be resolute yet able to overcome is also a virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue takes many forms, not all of equal weight; resoluteness that can overcome is also a virtue.

sentences.zh: 謹依諡法，布德行剛曰景，謂前議為允。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the law of posthumous names, 'spreading virtue with resolute conduct' is Jing; we consider the earlier proposal acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully following the law of posthumous names, 'spreading virtue with resolute conduct' is Jing; we hold the earlier proposal acceptable.

sentences.zh: 」司徙右長史張烈、主簿李枿刺稱：「按祉曆官累朝，當官允稱。

translations.literal: " Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education Zhang Lie and Registrar Li Wei submitted a memorial, saying: "Investigating Zhi's service across successive reigns, in office he was duly worthy.
translations.idiomatic: " Right chief clerk of the ministry of education Zhang Lie and registrar Li Wei submitted a memorial, saying, "Investigating Zhi's service across successive reigns, in office he was duly worthy.

sentences.zh: 委捍西南，邊隅靖遏，准行易名，獎誡攸在，竊謂無虧體例。

translations.literal: Entrusted to guard the southwest, he quieted and checked the border regions; assigning a name according to conduct to change the name -- reward and warning lie therein; we humbly consider there is no breach of precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted to guard the southwest, he quieted and checked the border regions; assigning a posthumous name according to conduct carries reward and warning alike; we humbly consider there is no breach of precedent.

sentences.zh: 」尚書李詔又述奏以府寺為允，靈太后可其奏。

translations.literal: " Minister Li Shao also submitted a memorial endorsing the offices' decision, and Empress Dowager Ling approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister Li Shao also memorialized endorsing the offices' view, and Empress Dowager Ling approved.

sentences.zh: 祉自當官，不憚強禦。

translations.literal: From the time Zhi took office, he did not fear the strong and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he took office, Zhi did not fear the powerful.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為剛斷，時有檢覆，每令出使。

translations.literal: The court considered him resolute and decisive; when there were investigations and reviews, he was always sent out on missions.
translations.idiomatic: The court considered him resolute and decisive; when investigations were needed he was always sent on missions.

sentences.zh: 然好慕刑名，頗為深文，所經之處，人號天狗下。

translations.literal: Yet he loved penal law and tended toward harsh interpretation; wherever he passed, people called him 'the heaven-dog descended.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved penal law and tended toward harsh interpretation; wherever he passed, people called him 'the heaven-dog descended.'

sentences.zh: 及出將臨州，並無恩潤，兵人患其嚴虐。

translations.literal: When he went out as general and governed a province, there was no kindness or generosity; soldiers and commoners suffered under his severity and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out as a general to govern a province he showed no kindness; soldiers and commoners suffered under his harsh cruelty.

sentences.zh: 子深。

translations.literal: His son Shen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen.

sentences.zh: 深字文泉，早有風尚，學涉經史，兼長几案。

translations.literal: Shen, styled Wenquan, early developed fine tastes; his learning ranged through the classics and histories, and he was also skilled at desk work.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, styled Wenquan, had refined tastes from youth; his learning ranged through the classics and histories, and he was also skilled at administrative work.

sentences.zh: 少與隴西李神俊同志相友。

translations.literal: In youth he was kindred in spirit and friends with Li Shenjun of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a kindred spirit and close friend of Li Shenjun of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 自司空記室參軍，再遷尚書駕部郎中。

translations.literal: Starting as Recorder of the Ministry of Works, he was twice promoted to Director of the Chariot Section in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as recorder of the ministry of works, he was promoted twice to director of the chariot section in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 于時沙汰郎官，務精才實，深以才堪見留。

translations.literal: At that time the director posts were being sifted for talent and substance; Shen was retained on account of his ability.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the director posts were being sifted for talent and substance; Shen was retained on account of his ability.

sentences.zh: 在公明斷，尚書僕射崔亮、吏部尚書甄琛咸敬重之。

translations.literal: In public affairs he was clear and decisive; Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Liang and Minister of Personnel Zhen Chen all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and decisive in public affairs, he was respected by vice director Cui Liang and minister of personnel Zhen Chen.

sentences.zh: 明帝行釋奠之禮，講《孝經》，深儕輩中獨蒙引聽，時論美之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming performed the sacrifice at the academy and lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, Shen alone among his peers was invited to attend; public opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming performed the academy sacrifice and lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, Shen alone among his peers was invited to attend, and public opinion praised this.

sentences.zh: 正光末，北地人車金雀等率羌、胡反叛，高平賊宿勤明達寇豳、破諸州，北海王顥為都督、行台討之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang, Che Jinque of Beidi and others led Qiang and Hu in rebellion; the Gaoping bandit Suqin Mingda raided Bin and devastated several prefectures; Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao was made commander and mobile headquarters to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang era, Che Jinque of Beidi and others led Qiang and Hu in rebellion; the Gaoping bandit Suqin Mingda raided Bin and devastated several prefectures; Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao was made commander and mobile headquarters to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 以深為行台右丞、軍司，仍領郎中。

translations.literal: Shen was made Right Vice Director of the Mobile Headquarters and army chief of staff, while still holding his director post.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was made right vice director of the mobile headquarters and army chief of staff while retaining his director post.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，還京。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Shen returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤反，攻圍華州，王平、薛鳳賢等作逆。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin rebelled, attacked and besieged Hua Province; Wang Ping, Xue Fengxian, and others joined the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin rebelled, attacked and besieged Hua Province, and Wang Ping, Xue Fengxian, and others rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 敕深兼給事黃門侍郎，與大行台、僕射長孫承業共會潼關，規模進止。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shen concurrently Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates; he joined the Great Mobile Headquarters Vice Director Changsun Chengye at Tong Pass to plan strategy and movements.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Shen was appointed concurrently attendant gentleman of the yellow gates; he joined great mobile headquarters vice director Changsun Chengye at Tong Pass to plan strategy and movements.

sentences.zh: 事平，以功賜爵新泰男。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xintai for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was put down, he was enfeoffed as baron of Xintai for his service.

sentences.zh: 靈太后曾幸芒山，集僧尼齋會，公卿盡在坐。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling once visited Mount Mang, gathering monks and nuns for a vegetarian feast; the high ministers were all present.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling once visited Mount Mang for a gathering of monks and nuns; every high minister was in attendance.

sentences.zh: 太后引見深，欣然勞問之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager summoned Shen before her and graciously inquired after him with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned Shen and graciously inquired after him.

sentences.zh: 顧謂左右曰：「羊深真忠臣也。

translations.literal: Turning to those beside her she said: "Yang Shen is a true loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to those beside her, she said, "Yang Shen is a true loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 」舉坐傾心。

translations.literal: " All present were deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: " All present were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 莊帝踐阼，除太府卿，又為二兗行台。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang ascended the throne, Shen was appointed Grand Minister of the Treasury and also made mobile headquarters of the two Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, he was appointed grand minister of the treasury and made mobile headquarters of the two Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 深處分軍國，損益隨機，亦有時譽。

translations.literal: Shen handled military and state affairs, adjusting gains and losses as circumstances required, and won some contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: He managed military and civil affairs, adapting policy to circumstances, and won some contemporary praise.

sentences.zh: 初爾硃榮殺害朝士，深第七弟侃為太山太守。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong first massacred court officials, Shen's seventh younger brother Kan was Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong first massacred court officials, Shen's seventh younger brother Kan was administrator of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 性粗武，遂率鄉人外招梁寇。

translations.literal: Rough and martial by nature, he then led local men to summon Liang invaders from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Rough and martial by nature, he led local men to invite Liang invaders from outside.

sentences.zh: 深在彭城，忽得侃書，招深同逆。

translations.literal: Shen was at Pengcheng when he suddenly received a letter from Kan inviting him to join the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was at Pengcheng when he suddenly received a letter from Kan inviting him to rebel together.

sentences.zh: 深慨然流涕，斬使人，並收表聞。

translations.literal: Shen sighed in grief and wept; he executed the messenger and submitted a memorial reporting the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Shen sighed, wept, executed the messenger, and submitted a memorial reporting the matter.

sentences.zh: 莊帝乃下詔褒其忠烈，令還朝受敕。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang then issued an edict praising his loyalty and valor, ordering him to return to court to receive commands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang then issued an edict praising his loyalty and ordered him back to court.

sentences.zh: 乃歸京師，除名。

translations.literal: He then returned to the capital and was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital and was dismissed from his post.

sentences.zh: 久之，除金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以深兼黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Shen was made concurrently Yellow Gates Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Shen was appointed concurrently vice director of the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 景平，免官。

translations.literal: When the situation was settled, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the revolt was crushed, he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，為散騎常侍、衛將軍、右光祿大夫，監起居注。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he served as Regular Attendant, Guard General, Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and supervised the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Putai era he was regular attendant, guard general, and right grand master of splendid happiness, and supervised the daily records.

sentences.zh: 自天下多事，東西二省，官員委積。

translations.literal: Since the realm was beset with troubles, the eastern and western secretariats had accumulated a glut of officials.
translations.idiomatic: With turmoil across the realm, the eastern and western secretariats had accumulated far too many officials.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝敕深與常侍盧道虔、元晏、元法壽選人補定，自奉朝請以上，各有沙汰。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin ordered Shen, Regular Attendant Lu Daoqian, Yuan Yan, and Yuan Fashou to select men to fill and fix appointments; from Court Gentleman upward, each rank was sifted and culled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiemin ordered Shen, regular attendant Lu Daoqian, Yuan Yan, and Yuan Fashou to review appointments; from court gentleman upward, each rank was sifted.

sentences.zh: 尋兼侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he was made concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝甚親待之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin treated him with great intimacy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiemin treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 時膠序廢替，名教陵遲。

translations.literal: At the time schools were abandoned and neglected, and moral teaching declined.
translations.idiomatic: Schools had fallen into neglect, and Confucian moral teaching was in decline.

sentences.zh: 深乃上疏，請修立國學，廣延胄子，帝善之。

translations.literal: Shen submitted a memorial requesting the restoration of the National Academy and the broad enrollment of noble scions; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shen submitted a memorial asking to restore the national academy and enroll more noble scions; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，除中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was appointed director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年，以深兼御史中尉、東道軍司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, Shen was made concurrently Censor Commander and eastern-route army chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was made concurrently censor commander and eastern-route army chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 及帝入關，深與樊子鵠不從齊神武，起兵於兗州，子鵠署深為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the passes, Shen and Fan Zihu refused to follow Qi Shenwu and raised troops in Yan Province; Zihu appointed Shen Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew into the passes, Shen and Fan Zihu refused to follow Gao Huan and raised troops in Yan Province; Zihu appointed Shen inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 天平二年正月，東魏軍討破之，斬於陣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tianping, Eastern Wei troops defeated them and beheaded him in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Tianping, Eastern Wei troops routed them and beheaded him on the field.

sentences.zh: 深子肅，武定末儀同、開府、東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: Shen's son Su, at the end of Wuding held ceremonial equal rank, opened office, and was Director of the Eastern Pavilion Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's son Su, by the end of the Wuding era, held ceremonial equal rank with an opened office and served as director of the eastern pavilion academy.

sentences.zh: 以學尚知名。

translations.literal: He was known for scholarly pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，為冀州中從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ganming he was Chief Clerk of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Ganming era he was chief clerk of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王為巡省大使，肅以遲緩不任職解。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhao was touring-inspection envoy, Su was dismissed for sluggishness and unsuitability for office.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Zhao served as touring-inspection envoy, Su was dismissed for sluggishness and failure to perform his duties.

sentences.zh: 朝議以肅無罪，尋復之。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Su was not guilty, and before long he was reinstated.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged him innocent, and he was soon reinstated.

sentences.zh: 武平中，入文林館撰書。

translations.literal: During Wuping he entered the Wenlin Academy to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuping era he entered the Wenlin Academy to compile books.

sentences.zh: 尋為武德郡守。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Administrator of Wude Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made administrator of Wude Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祉弟靈引，好法律。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Lingyin loved the law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Lingyin had a passion for the law.

sentences.zh: 李彪為中丞，以為書侍御史，固辭，彪頗銜之。

translations.literal: When Li Biao was censor-in-chief, he wanted to appoint him Palace Attendant Censor; Lingyin firmly declined, and Biao bore considerable resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Biao was censor-in-chief, he wanted to appoint him palace attendant censor; Lingyin firmly declined, and Biao resented it.

sentences.zh: 及為三公郎，坐兄祉事知而不糾，彪劾奏免官。

translations.literal: When he became a director in the Three Excellencies office, he was charged with knowing of his brother Zhi's affair yet failing to investigate; Biao impeached him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When he became a director in the three excellencies office, he was charged with knowing of his brother Zhi's misconduct yet failing to investigate; Biao impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 甚為尚書令高肇所昵。

translations.literal: He was greatly favored by Minister of the Secretariat Gao Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Secretariat Gao Zhao favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 京兆王愉與肇深相嫌忌。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingzhao Yuan Yu and Gao Zhao deeply detested each other.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingzhao Yuan Yu and Gao Zhao deeply detested each other.

sentences.zh: 及愉出鎮冀州，肇與靈引為愉長史，以相間伺。

translations.literal: When Yu went out to govern Ji Province as military commander, Gao Zhao had Lingyin serve as Yu's chief administrator to spy on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu went out to govern Ji Province, Gao Zhao installed Lingyin as Yu's chief administrator to spy on him.

sentences.zh: 靈引私恃肇勢，每折於愉。

translations.literal: Lingyin privately relied on Gao Zhao's power, yet was repeatedly overruled by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyin privately relied on Gao Zhao's backing, yet Yu repeatedly overruled him.

sentences.zh: 及愉作逆，先斬靈引於門。

translations.literal: When Yu rebelled, he first beheaded Lingyin at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu rebelled, he beheaded Lingyin at the gate first.

sentences.zh: 時論云：「非直愉自不臣，抑亦由肇及靈引所致。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion said: "It was not only that Yu himself was disloyal; it was also brought about by Gao Zhao and Lingyin.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held: "It was not only that Yu himself was disloyal; Gao Zhao and Lingyin brought it about as well.

sentences.zh: 」事平，贈平東將軍、兗州刺史，諡曰威。

translations.literal: " When the affair was settled, Lingyin was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yan Province, with posthumous name Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " When the rebellion was put down, he was posthumously granted general who pacifies the east and inspector of Yan Province, with posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 子敦，字元禮，性尚閑素，學涉書史。

translations.literal: His son Dun, styled Yuanli, by nature favored quiet simplicity; his learning ranged through books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dun, styled Yuanli, favored quiet simplicity; his learning ranged through books and histories.

sentences.zh: 以父死王中，除給事中。

translations.literal: Because his father died in the prince's rebellion, he was appointed Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father died in the prince's rebellion, he was appointed attendant within the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 出為本州別駕。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Vice Governor of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as vice governor of his native province.

sentences.zh: 公平正直，見非法，終不判署。

translations.literal: Fair and upright, when he saw what was unlawful he never would sign approval.
translations.idiomatic: Fair and upright, he never signed approval for anything unlawful.

sentences.zh: 後為衛將軍、廣平太守，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Later he served as Guard General and Administrator of Guangping, winning a strong reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as guard general and administrator of Guangping and won a strong reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 奸吏局蹐，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: Corrupt clerks cowered; not the slightest thing was violated.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks cowered before him; nothing was violated, however small.

sentences.zh: 雅性清儉，屬歲饑，家饋未至，使人外尋陂澤，采藕根食之。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and frugal; during a year of famine, before household provisions arrived, he sent men to search ponds and marshes and gathered lotus roots to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and frugal by nature, during a famine year, before household provisions arrived, he sent men to search ponds and marshes and gathered lotus roots to eat.

sentences.zh: 遇有疾苦，家人解衣質米以供之。

translations.literal: When he encountered the sick and suffering, his family pawned their clothes for rice to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: When he met the sick and destitute, his family pawned their clothes for rice to help them.

sentences.zh: 然政尚威嚴。

translations.literal: Yet his governance emphasized stern authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his rule emphasized stern authority.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其清白，賜穀一千斛，絹一百匹。

translations.literal: The court, on account of his integrity, granted him a thousand bushels of grain and a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded his integrity with a thousand bushels of grain and a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 卒官，吏人奔哭，莫不悲慟。

translations.literal: He died in office; officials and commoners rushed to weep, none without grief.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; officials and commoners rushed to mourn, and all were stricken with grief.

sentences.zh: 贈衛大將軍、吏部尚書、兗州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Great General of the Guard, Minister of Personnel, and Inspector of Yan Province, with posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted great general of the guard, minister of personnel, and inspector of Yan Province, with posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 武定初，齊神武以敦及中山太守蘇淑在官奉法，清約自居，宜見追褒，仍上言請加旌錄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, Qi Shenwu held that Dun and Zhongshan Administrator Su Shu, in office obeyed the law and kept themselves pure and frugal, and deserved posthumous praise; he submitted a memorial requesting commendation and record.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wuding era, Gao Huan felt that Dun and Zhongshan administrator Su Shu had served the law faithfully and lived in austere integrity, and deserved posthumous praise; he submitted a memorial asking that they be commended and recorded.

sentences.zh: 詔各賞帛一百匹，粟五百斛，下郡國，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: An edict awarded each a hundred bolts of silk and five hundred bushels of grain, sent down to the commanderies and kingdoms so all would hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded each a hundred bolts of silk and five hundred bushels of grain and circulated the decree through the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 靈引弟瑩，字靈珍，兗州別駕從事。

translations.literal: Lingyin's younger brother Ying, styled Lingzhen, was Attendant Clerk to the Vice Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyin's younger brother Ying, styled Lingzhen, was attendant clerk to the vice governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 子烈。

translations.literal: His son Lie.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lie.

sentences.zh: 烈字信卿，少通敏，頗自修立，有成人風。

translations.literal: Lie, styled Xinqing, was clever and quick from youth, cultivated himself diligently, and had the bearing of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: Lie, styled Xinqing, was clever and quick from youth, disciplined himself carefully, and had the bearing of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，能言名理，以玄學知名。

translations.literal: He loved reading, could discourse on principle, and was known for Neo-Daoist learning.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading, could discourse on principle, and was known for Neo-Daoist learning.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌末，烈從兄侃為太山太守，據郡起兵外叛。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang under Wei, Lie's cousin Kan was Administrator of Taishan; he seized the commandery and raised troops in rebellion against the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochang era, Lie's cousin Kan was administrator of Taishan; he seized the commandery and rebelled against the court.

sentences.zh: 烈潛知共謀，深懼家禍，與從兄廣平太守敦馳赴洛陽告難。

translations.literal: Lie secretly learned of the conspiracy and deeply feared disaster for his clan; with his cousin Guangping Administrator Dun he raced to Luoyang to report the danger.
translations.idiomatic: Lie secretly learned of the plot and feared disaster for his clan; with his cousin Dun, administrator of Guangping, he raced to Luoyang to report the danger.

sentences.zh: 朝廷將加厚賞，烈告人云：「譬如斬手全軀，所存者大故爾，豈有幸從兄之敗，以為己利乎。

translations.literal: When the court was about to grant him a rich reward, Lie told others: "It is like cutting off a hand to save the whole body; what remains is the greater thing, that is all. How could I rejoice in my cousin's defeat to profit myself?
translations.idiomatic: When the court was about to reward him generously, Lie said: "It is like cutting off a hand to save the whole body; the greater part is preserved, that is all. How could I welcome my cousin's downfall to profit myself?

sentences.zh: 」卒無所受。

translations.literal: " In the end he accepted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he accepted nothing.

sentences.zh: 天保中，累遷尚書祠部、左右戶郎中，在官咸為稱職。

translations.literal: During Tianbao he was promoted through Director of the Sacrifices Section and Director of the Left and Right Household Sections in the Secretariat; in every post he was judged competent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he rose through director of the sacrifices section and director of the left and right household sections; in every post he was judged competent.

sentences.zh: 除陽平太守，有能名。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Yangping and won a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Yangping and won a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 時頻有災蝗，犬牙不入陽平境，敕書褒美焉。

translations.literal: Locust disasters struck repeatedly, yet the swarms never crossed into Yangping; an imperial edict praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Locust plagues struck repeatedly, yet the swarms never crossed into Yangping; an imperial edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿少卿、兗州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Household and Chief Arbiter of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the imperial household and chief arbiter of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 天平初，除義州刺史，以老還鄉，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was appointed Inspector of Yi Province; owing to age he returned home and died there.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianping era he was appointed inspector of Yi Province; in old age he returned home and died there.

sentences.zh: 烈家傳素業，閨門修飭，為世所稱。

translations.literal: Lie's family transmitted plain virtue through generations; their inner household was disciplined and praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Lie family passed down plain virtue from generation to generation; their household conduct was disciplined and widely praised.

sentences.zh: 一門女不再醮。

translations.literal: Not one woman in the clan remarried.
translations.idiomatic: No woman in the clan ever remarried.

sentences.zh: 魏太和中，於兗州造一尼寺，女寡居無子者，並出家為尼，咸存戒行。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of Wei they built a nunnery in Yan Province; women who were widowed and childless all took the tonsure as nuns and kept the precepts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era they built a nunnery in Yan Province; widowed women without sons all became nuns and kept the precepts.

sentences.zh: 烈天統中與尚書畢義雲爭兗州大中正。

translations.literal: During Tiantong, Lie contested the chief arbiter post of Yan Province with Minister of the Secretariat Bi Yiyun.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiantong era Lie contested the chief arbiter post of Yan Province with minister of the secretariat Bi Yiyun.

sentences.zh: 義雲盛稱門代累世，本州刺史，卿世為我家故史。

translations.literal: Yiyun greatly vaunted his family's generations of office and said: "Your ancestors for generations were our family's old retainers when we were governors of this province."
translations.idiomatic: Yiyun vaunted his family's generations of office: "For generations your clan were retainers in my family's service when we governed this province."

sentences.zh: 烈云：「自畢軌被誅以還，寂無人物。

translations.literal: Lie said: "Since Bi Gui was executed, your house has been empty of distinguished men.
translations.idiomatic: Lie said: "Since Bi Gui was executed, your house has produced no one of note.

sentences.zh: 近日刺史，皆疆場之上，彼此而得，何足為言。

translations.literal: The recent governors were men who gained their posts back and forth across the battle lines; what is there to boast of?
translations.idiomatic: Your recent governors won their posts back and forth on the frontier; hardly worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 豈若我之漢河南尹、晉朝太傅，名德學行，百世傳美。

translations.literal: How can that compare with our Han dynasty Governor of Henan and Jin dynasty Grand Tutor, whose fame, virtue, learning, and conduct have been praised for a hundred generations?
translations.idiomatic: How does that compare with our governor of Henan under Han and grand tutor under Jin, whose fame, virtue, learning, and conduct have been praised for a hundred generations?

sentences.zh: 且男清女貞，足以相冠，自外多可稱也。

translations.literal: Moreover our men are pure and our women chaste, enough to put us above you; apart from that, much else can be praised as well.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover our men are pure and our women chaste, enough to set us above you, and much else besides is worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 」蓋譏義雲之帷薄焉。

translations.literal: " This was presumably to ridicule the moral failings of Yiyun's household.
translations.idiomatic: " This was apparently a jibe at the lax moral conduct of Yiyun's household.

sentences.zh: 烈弟修，有才幹，卒于尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Lie's younger brother Xiu had talent and ability; he died while serving as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's younger brother Xiu was talented and capable; he died while serving as left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子玄正。

translations.literal: His son Xuanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanzheng.

sentences.zh: 武平末，將作丞。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuping era he was director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang of Sui he was Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui he was vice director of the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 卒於隴西郡贊務。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Administrative Aide of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as administrative aide of Longxi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 論曰：薛安都一武夫耳，雖輕於去就，實啟東南。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Xue Andou was only a military man; though light in his choices of side, he truly opened the way in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Xue Andou was only a fighting man; though fickle in his allegiances, he truly opened the way in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 事窘圖變，而竟保寵祿，優矣。

translations.literal: When affairs grew desperate he sought change, yet in the end kept favor and stipend; well done indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When cornered he adapted, yet in the end kept favor and stipend; no small feat.

sentences.zh: 休賓窮而委質；

translations.literal: Xiubin, cornered, submitted his loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin, brought to extremity, submitted his loyalty;

sentences.zh: 孝標名重東南；

translations.literal: Xiaobiao's fame weighed heavily in the southeast;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobiao's name carried great weight in the southeast;

sentences.zh: 法壽拓落不羈，克昌厥後；

translations.literal: Fashou was free-spirited and unrestrained, and he made his posterity flourish;
translations.idiomatic: Fashou was free-spirited and unrestrained, and his line flourished after him;

sentences.zh: 景伯兄弟儒素，良可稱乎。

translations.literal: The Jingbo brothers were scholarly and plain; truly worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingbo brothers were scholarly and plain; truly worth praise.

sentences.zh: 眾敬舉地納誠，榮曜朝國；

translations.literal: Zhongjing offered the land and pledged loyalty, bringing glory to the court and realm;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing offered the land and pledged loyalty, bringing glory to court and kingdom;

sentences.zh: 人位並列，無乏于時。

translations.literal: Men and offices stood side by side, never wanting in their day.
translations.idiomatic: Men and offices stood side by side, never wanting in their day.

sentences.zh: 羊祉剛酷之風，得死為幸。

translations.literal: Yang Zhi's harsh and cruel temperament; to die was his good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi's harsh and cruel temperament; to die was his good fortune.

sentences.zh: 深以才幹從事，聲跡可稱。

translations.literal: Shen served by talent and ability; his reputation and deeds are worth mention.
translations.idiomatic: Shen served through talent and ability; his reputation and deeds deserve mention.

sentences.zh: 敦、烈持己所遵，殆時彥也。

translations.literal: Dun and Lie held to the principles they followed; nearly men of the age's finest.
translations.idiomatic: Dun and Lie held to the principles they lived by; nearly the finest men of their age.
